De la Fuente beat Mikel Arteta, Luis Enrique and Unai Emery to the award

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente has won the Men’s Coach of the Year award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London.

De la Fuente guided Spain to glory at the World Cup this summer, which saw La Roja be crowned world champions for the second time. The 65-year-old also won Euro 2024 with Spain.

He overcame competition from a host of Europe’s best managers, including Premer League winner with Arsenal Mikel Arteta.

Champions League winner Luis Enrique also missed out on the award, as well as Bundesliga champion Vincent Kompany and Europa League winner Unai Emery.

articles.content:
Ballon d’Or 2026: Follow the results live from London

The latest updates from the Ballon d'Or 2026

Last Update:

The most prestigious individual prizes in football are being handed out in London as the 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place on Monday.

The award has been co-organised with UEFA since 2024, with Aitana Bonmati and Ousmane Dembele lifting the headline women’s and men’s honours in 2025.

Spain and London City Lionesses schemer Alexia Putellas and Bayern Munich and England talisman Harry Kane are being tipped to win the main individual awards this year. Follow the latest with our live coverage.

20:22 GMT: De la Fuente wins coach award

Luis de la Fuente is the winner of the Men’s Coach of the Year award! The Spaniard guided his country to a World Cup triumph for only the second time.

21:15 GMT: Men’s award up next

After a scheduled commercial break, we will find out who the Men’s Coach of the Year winner is. The nominees feature two current Premier League managers among a five-manager shortlist:

21:10 GMT: Pere Romeu named women’s coach winner

It’s been a great night for Barcelona so far as they continue their clean sweep of the awards so far as Barcelona women manager wins the Women’s Coach of the Year.

Romeu guided Barcelona to a triumph in the Women’s Champions League and won Liga F for the second successive time.

21:00 GMT: Lopez wins women’s youngster award

It is also back-to-back awards for a Barcelona player in the women’s Young Talent award as Vicky Lopez scoops up the award once again!

20:50 GMT: Yamal scoops young player of the year award

The first award, the Young Talent of the Year, has gone to one of the favourites in the Men’s Player of the Year award Lamine Yamal, who has scooped up the award for the third time.

Could this mean the main award is going to either Kane or Mbappe?

20:45 GMT: We are finally underway!

Some 45 minutes later than planned, seemingly due to the central London traffic, the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony is underway, with British singer Jorja Smith kicking things off with a performance.

Stay tuned for all the latest updates as they happen. A reminder of all the winners that will be announced tonight:

20:25 GMT: ‘Definitely my best season ever’ says Kane

articles.content:
Ballon d’Or 2026 Men’s Young Player of the Year 2026: Yamal scoops award for third time

Yamal was considered a contender to win the 2026 Men's Player of the Year award

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal has been named the Men’s Young Talent of the Year for the third year running at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards in London.

Yamal, 19, is a contender to win the Men’s Ballon d’Or Player of the Year winner, with this success suggesting he is set to miss out on the full award to one of the other two favourites: Harry Kane or Kylian Mbappe.

The teenager was instrumental in Spain’s World Cup win in the summer, which was his second major international honour after also winning Euro 2024, while he won LaLiga with Barca.

After accepting the award, Yamal nervously laughed off asked by co-host Thierry Henry whether this wasn’t the award he wanted to win, before adding: “It is an honour to be here and receive this prize.

“I would have liked to see my team-mate Cubarsi here because I think this prize should have been for him. He has been playing at an excellent level for some time.

“This is my third year up here for this prize. I would like to thank my club and my national team.

“Speaking about this one specifically, this one should have been for Curbasi.”

articles.content:
Chaos at the Ballon d’Or! Statement released after Kane, Mbappe, Yamal and Messi all announced as winners

Last Update:

The Ballon d’Or were forced to release a statement after accidentally publishing several articles on their official site all announcing different winners ahead of Monday’s ceremony.

Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe all had articles published on them winning the coveted award, with the three articles later deleted.

A subsequent statement from a Ballon d’Or spokesperson said: “Portraits of some Ballon d’Or nominees prepared by Ballondor.com were inadvertently published online.

“These articles had been prepared in advance for all nominees in the event of a win. They DO NOT, in any way, reveal the podium, which remains unknown to everyone at this time.”

The Ballon d’Or ceremony, hosted in London, has now been pushed back to 8:30pm GMT, which is unknown to be a result of the article mistakes.

Ballon d’Or”: Kane prematurely named winner

An article naming Harry Kane as the winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or began circulating online shortly after 17:15 GMT on Monday, more than four hours before the ceremony was due to begin at London’s Palladium Theatre.

The piece, published on the award’s official website, sparked confusion over whether organisers France Football had accidentally revealed the winner after journalists voted at the end of September.

However, further investigation revealed similar articles had also been published for other leading contenders, including Barcelona’s Yamal and Real Madrid’s Mbappe.

articles.content:
What time is the Ballon d’Or ceremony 2026? Full start details, confirmed timings

All the details on Ballon d'Or 2026 timings

Last Update:

Created by France Football in 1956, the most prestigious individual prizes in football will be awarded in London when the 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place on Monday.

The award has been co-organised with UEFA since 2024, with Aitana Bonmati and Ousmane Dembele lifting the headline women’s and men’s honours in 2025.

Spain and London City Lionesses schemer Alexia Putellas is being tipped to end Barcelona and Roja magician Bonmati’s three-year run in the Ballon d’Or Feminin this time.

Bayern Munich and England talisman Harry Kane is the favourite in the men’s category after an extraordinarily prolific year, ahead of Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe, who won the Golden Boot at the World Cup 2026 with France and top-scored in La Liga last season.

What time is the Ballon d’Or 2026?

Here are the key scheduled timings for the ceremony.

When does the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony start?

Here are the scheduled start times for the ceremony. You can also visit the Ballon d’Or worldwide timings list.

Why is the Ballon d’Or 2026 in London?

Paris’ Theatre du Chatelet has hosted the Ballon d’Or since 2019 but the ceremony will move to the London Palladium this year.

The first Ballon d’Or ceremony in London is a tribute to Sir Stanley Matthews, the English inaugural recipient of the golden ball.

L’Equipe editor Gabriel Hanot gave Matthews the award on December 18 1956 in a wood-panelled room at Blackpool Town Hall. Matthews is said to have responded with a “truncated speech” and received a “smattering of applause”.

“He was a pioneer,” the Ballon d’Or’s official account says of Matthews.

“Continually pushing the boundaries in diet and fitness and adopting methodologies that, at the time, were considered quirky at best by scoffing team-mates, but which are now cornerstones of modern-day practices.

“He was years ahead of the curve. Decades. And though it was only a ceremony of sorts, and though this year’s gala is being held 250 miles south of the Lancashire coastline, it can be stated that this autumn football is coming home. Back to where the Ballon d’Or all began.”

Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony: Who’s hosting and performing?

Hugely popular journalist Kate Scott will be on expert hosting duties alongside familiar CBS Sports sidekick Thierry Henry.

France legend Henry was nominated for the Ballon d’Or nine times, finishing second in 2003.

Musicians Jorja Smith and French Montana will perform and organisers are promising “further surprises”.

British singer-songwriter Smith blends R&B, soul, jazz and electronic influences and will open the ceremony by performing her 2016 single, Blue Lights, to mark 10 years since the release of the record.

Morocco-born, Bronx raised Montana is a three-time Grammy-nominated hiphop star whose hits include the Diamond-certified Unforgettable, which featured Swae Lee, the five-time Platinum No Stylist with Drake and the six-time Platinum Lockjaw with Kodak Black.

articles.summary: Harry Kane is likely to pip Kylian Mbappe,  Lamine Yamal and Lionel Messi and win the Ballon d'Or tonight...
articles.content:
Ballon d’Or 2026: Odds, stats and where to watch with Harry Kane favourite to win ahead of Kylian Mbappe, Lamine Yamal and Lionel Messi

Harry Kane is likely to pip Kylian Mbappe,  Lamine Yamal and Lionel Messi and win the Ballon d'Or tonight...

Last Update:

Harry Kane is expected to become just the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London tonight.

The Bayern Munich striker is the bookmakers’ favourite to be crowned the world’s best player at a glittering event – hosted by Thierry Henry and Kate Scott – at the Palladium Theatre.

Kane has had another wonderful year for Bayern and England, scoring 61 times for the Bundesliga giants in all competitions last season as they clinched another league and cup double. The 33-year-old also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

Kylian Mbappe is thought to be Kane’s closest challenger. Mbappe scored 42 goals in 44 games for Real Madrid last season, and added another 10 in the United States, Canada and Mexico over the summer. But Madrid’s failure to land any major silverware could hamper his chances.

He will also arrive in London with a spring in his step after netting twice in Madrid’s Clasico win at Barcelona last night.

The same can’t be said for Lamine Yamal, who was on the losing side at Camp Nou. The teenager is regarded as third favourite to lift the trophy despite scoring 16 times as Barca retained the Liga trophy and playing a key role as Spain backed up their 2024 European Championship success by winning the World Cup.

Lionel Messi is believed to be an outsider.

Messi returned to the shortlist for the first time in three years following his remarkable performances at the World Cup, where he guided Argentina to the final before losing to Spain.

The 39-year-old also had another brilliant year with Inter Miami in the United States, helping them win a maiden MLS Cup in December.

Messi has won the award eight times previously but it would be a major surprise if he were to add a ninth.

If Kane does triumph he will join Kevin Keegan, Sir Bobby Charlton, Sir Stanley Matthews and Michael Owen in a small group of English winners.

How does the voting for the Ballon d’Or work?

The 30-player shortlist for the main awards is voted for by a panel of journalists from France Football and L’Equipe.

One journalist from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings then votes for their top 10 from each list with each position afforded a certain number of points.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo needs Saudi Pro League to decide on 982nd career goal
articles.summary: Officials are assessing a potential Cristiano Ronaldo goal
articles.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo needs Saudi Pro League to decide on 982nd career goal

Officials are assessing a potential Cristiano Ronaldo goal

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo may have to wait for his 982nd career goal if a Saudi Pro League meeting on Monday decides that the Al-Nassr captain’s header in his side’s 3-1 top-flight win at Al-Faisaly on Friday was an own-goal.

Five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo ran to celebrate after competing with opposition defender Andrei Girotto to apply the touch that diverted Joao Felix’s cross off a post and in for Al-Nassr’s second goal of the game, although replays appear to make the 41-year-old’s claim to have scored unclear.

Tariq Kayyal, the head of the league’s Compliance Committee, says officials are waiting on referee Abdullah Al-Owaidan’s statement and plan to “study all the reports”.

Will Cristiano Ronaldo be awarded Al Nassr goal?

While the Saudi Pro League highlights of the game suggest Ronaldo has been credited with the goal – the video is titled “Ronaldo gets GOAL 982” – official data providers appear to have attributed Girotto with the final touch.

“If we are convinced by them, we will decide whether to uphold or reject the decision, thus awarding the goal with the correct ruling,” Kayyal said of the perspectives his committee will consider, via Al-Riyadh.

Pundit and former Saudi Arabia midfielder Khalid Al-Shenaif reportedly said a refereeing committee had given the goal to Ronaldo.

Al-Shenaif is said to have claimed that the league has contacted data providers including experts Opta, “international platforms” and “possibly FIFA” to emphasise that the Madrid all-time top scorer headed the ball.

“That settles the matter,” The Nassr Tribune quoted Al-Shenaif as saying. “His tally stands at 982 goals.

“I believe the Saudi Pro League – or perhaps the Saudi Football Federation – will contact Opta… whose statistics are published across platforms worldwide, to confirm that the goal belongs to Ronaldo in accordance with the [refereeing committee verdict].”

On Monday morning, Opta’s match centre for the game credited Girotto with an own-goal.

How many goals has Cristiano Ronaldo scored?

Ronaldo scored his 981st career goal in a 3-1 home win over Uzbekistan Super League team Neftchi Fergana in the AFC Champions League on October 12.

As well as the enduring debate about whether Ronaldo or generational rival Lionel Messi is the best player of modern times, the Portugal icon’s status as the highest scorer ever has been questioned by some who consider Pele the leading marksman in history.

“All the goals [of mine] have videos,” Ronaldo told former Manchester United teammate Rio Ferdinand in 2024. “I will prove to the people, if they prefer this player… I don’t care about that.”

When will Cristiano Ronaldo score his 1,000th goal?

Speaking before the start of Portugal’s Nations League campaign in September, Ronaldo was asked whether he would prefer his 1,000th goal to be for Al-Nassr or Portugal.

“You know the answer: for the national team,” he replied. “It would be the culmination of a beautiful story. As the coach said: the cherry on top of the cake.”

The first camp under Portugal’s new head coach, Jorge Jesus, who led Al-Nassr to the Saudi title last season, ended in premature and acrimonious fashion for Ronaldo.

Having started Portugal’s first game at home to Wales, Ronaldo left the camp after remaining an unused substitute away to Norway on September 27 and discovering he would not start in Denmark on October 1.

In an elaborate statement, Ronaldo then said Jorge Jesus twice “broke his word” and committed an “absolute breach of trust”.

The Portuguese Football Federation has since given Ronaldo a 30-day suspension and fine of around £215 for the walk-out.

With Al-Nassr less than a third of the way through their season, Portugal in action less regularly and Ronaldo’s international future in doubt, his 1,000th goal is likeliest to arrive in this season’s Saudi Pro League.

Cristiano Ronaldo net worth

On financial website Forbes’ all-time list of the highest earning athletes in a year, only boxer Floyd Mayweather eclipses Ronaldo, having pocketed an estimated $300 million (£226m) in 2015 and $285m (£214.5m) in 2018.

Ronaldo was said to have surpassed $1 billion (£771m) in career earnings two years before becoming the most high-profile footballer to move to Saudi Arabia, making his Al-Nassr debut in January 2023.

Ronaldo’s first Al-Nassr deal was widely reported to be worth £14.75m a month or £3.4m per week. His annual salary was said to be £177m per year, made up of £62m for his football salary, supplemented by commercial bonuses.

Ronaldo has a variety of lucrative sponsorship deals, with his recent endorsements including Whoop, video game UFL and cryptocurrency exchange Binance.

Ronaldo won the Saudi title for the first time last season but failed to top-score in the top flight for the first time in his three seasons of being involved.

Shortly after Al-Nassr finished third in 2025/26 – 13 points behind Al-Ittihad – Ronaldo appeared to strongly hint on social media that he had played his final game for the club.

He agreed a new contract exactly a month later, having scored in Portugal’s triumphant Nations League semi-final against Germany and final against Spain.

He missed three matches in all competitions earlier this year, with Real Madrid’s all-time top scorer thought to have been unhappy at Al-Nassr’s perceived lack of transfer activity.

When is Ronaldo playing next? Al Nassr vs Al Wasl off

The AFC announced on Sunday that Al-Nassr’s Champions League home game against UAE Pro League side Al-Wasl on Monday would be postponed.

No reason was given for the decision, although Reuters cited the intensification of fighting in Yemen between a Saudi-led coalition and Iran-aligned ​Houthi forces, who have recently targeted Saudi airports including Riyadh.

Saudi teams have travelled by road for matches in the competition. The outlet said it had contacted Al-Wasl and the ⁠AFC ​for comment.

The Saudi Arabian Football Federation released a statement on Sunday saying arrangements for the game had been completed, including flight permits for Al-Wasl and the club’s national FA and the arrival of the match commissioner and refereeing team in Riyadh.

The federation “affirmed full support” for Al-Nassr and Saudi clubs in international competitions, voicing its “readiness to provide all necessary support and assistance in any legal actions taken by the clubs to protect their rights”.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho gives Lamine Yamal verdict: ‘He tried everything’
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho called the referee in Barca vs Madrid 'great'
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho gives Lamine Yamal verdict: ‘He tried everything’

Jose Mourinho called the referee in Barca vs Madrid 'great'

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has called Real Madrid “extraordinary” after his side ended Barcelona’s perfect record in La Liga, singling out Marc Cucurella for coping with the “toughest match” of the full-back’s career against Ballon d’Or contender Lamine Yamal.

New signing Cucurella marked winger Yamal and played a part in the first of Kylian Mbappe’s goals in Madrid’s 2-1 away win, feeding Yan Diomande for a cross that was turned against the striker by opposition defender Gerard Martin’s attempted clearance.

“You can win by luck, by defending a lot… but we won comfortably and deservedly,” said Mourinho (via Marca), speaking after extinguishing Barca’s nine-match winning start to the Liga season to move three points behind the leaders.

“I’ve learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mentality to play. It’s a complete squad, they work hard, and they’re ready to win.”

Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Lamine Yamal ‘smart’

Spain sensation Yamal has eight goals and six assists in this season’s Liga but sent a glorious chance wide between Mbappe’s opener and the interval.

After Raphinha equalised during the second half, Yamal curled an effort wide and Mbappe struck his second to leave the 19-year-old looking rueful once the full-time whistle had sounded on the first clasico of the campaign.

“I always say that I only understand how good players are when I see them in front of me,” Mourinho said of the best result of his second spell in charge, having been reappointed before the start of the season.

“On television, I miss something. Ten metres away, I understand the quality of the players. [Yamal’s] very good, very difficult to play against.

“Besides being good, he’s smart. He tried everything. It’s the toughest match Cucu has had, against a very good player.”

Real Madrid boss Mourinho praises referee vs Barca

Mourinho warned that the win for Madrid, who are a point behind second-placed Atleti, will be meaningless if they do not prevail at midtable Racing Santander on Sunday (15:15 GMT).

“It was a great match,” said the Portuguese. “A high-level game – one that surely everyone who loves football stopped to watch, with two teams who played to win.

“I’m more concerned with speaking about my own team, but the lads played an extraordinary match – very organised, focused, with the courage to play out from the back against opponents who pressed a lot.

“We had chances to make it 2-0… Barcelona reacted strongly in the second half but we remained very calm and organised, and even at 1-1 we never lost our composure.

“Against great opponents and with a referee [Juan Martinez Munuera] who I think had a great game… it was a great match, a great victory.”

Real Madrid team vs Barcelona in el clasico

Andriy Lunin – who made several impressive saves – replaced Thibaut Courtois in one of five Madrid changes alongside the introductions of defenders Ibrahima Konate and Cucurella, midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni and winger Diomande.

Alvaro Carreras, Antonio Rudiger and Eduardo Camavinga moved to the bench. Vinicius Junior was suspended.

Newcastle, Brentford and Hull rose in the Premier League table

Newcastle visited Crystal Palace aiming to end a run of two consecutive defeats and Hull City were targeting a first win in seven matches in all competitions when the Tigers hosted Brentford on Sunday.

The Magpies had followed up a 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City with a 1-0 defeat at home to Aston Villa eight days earlier.

Palace had lost 5-0 at arch-rivals Brighton & Hove Albion a week earlier, while Brentford spurned a lead to suffer their first top-flight defeat of the season with a 2-1 home defeat to Liverpool on October 17.

You can also relive text updates as they happened from Sunday’s simultaneous games: Manchester United vs Bournemouth and Liverpool vs Brighton & Hove Albion.

articles.title: Wirtz on ankle injury and Liverpool win: ‘Things weren’t so good’
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz twisted his ankle in Liverpool vs Brighton
articles.content:
Wirtz on ankle injury and Liverpool win: ‘Things weren’t so good’

Florian Wirtz twisted his ankle in Liverpool vs Brighton

Last Update:

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz says he is ignoring people who “judge” him and is “even happier” with Sunday’s 2-0 win at home to Brighton & Hove Albion because of the Reds’ run of two victories in their first six league games of the season.

Seeking a first home league win since April 25, Liverpool took a 17th-minute lead when one of Wirtz’s Germany teammates, Pascal Gross, applied the deciding touch to the £116 million playmaker’s shot, followed by Alexander Isak striking his sixth Premier League goal of the season four minutes later.

“It’s really enjoyable, I have to say,” Wirtz told BBC Sport, also suggesting that he will not be sidelined by an ankle injury that caused his substitution.

“Many things weren’t so good in the last month, so I’m even happier that it’s going well at the moment. We are on a good [path] to get where we want to be.”

“We had the right mentality [against Brighton]. Especially in the, first half or the first 30 minutes, we were on top of them and really good in the duels, also creating a lot of chances.”

Liverpool vs Brighton: Wirtz ‘just wants to play’

Liverpool broke their club record at the time to sign Wirtz from Leverkusen in June 2025, making his return of five goals and three assists in 33 league appearances seem another underwhelming part of their meek title defence.

“Maybe I’m just an interesting guy,” Wirtz said of scrutiny around his displays. “I just play my football – if people want to talk about or judge me, that’s their job.

“I’m not focusing on that; I just want to play football and I cannot do more.”

Wirtz scored his first goal of the campaign in the 4-3 home win over Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“I would have preferred that the [first] goal [against Brighton] was given to me,” Wirtz reflected. “But it’s like this now.”

What’s next? Liverpool fixtures

Liverpool – perhaps without Wirtz – are next in action at home to Chelsea in the EFL Cup fourth round on October 28.

They then host defending champions Arsenal in the league on Sunday.

articles.title: ‘No hiding from tough situation’ says Carrick after latest Man Utd defeat
articles.summary: United are alarmingly close to the relegation zone
articles.content:
‘No hiding from tough situation’ says Carrick after latest Man Utd defeat

United are alarmingly close to the relegation zone

Last Update:

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said there could be ‘no hiding’ from him or his players after their latest poor result in the Premier League.

A 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth left United 16th in the top flight and without a win in eight matches.

Carrick was applauded by fans at the end who turned on the club’s board and Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, instead.

Carrick had taken the decision to leave out captain Bruno Fernandes – who stayed on the bench throughout.

Carrick applauded fans on a slow lap of Old Trafford but insisted afterwards that he was not saying goodbye.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion – the dynamic of what it was like today. Not for me personally but for Manchester United.

“I feel a lot of responsibility, I’ve been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful to to see us going through this at this moment in time.

“It wasn’t a farewell from me. I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment.

“It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know.

“I will always do my best for the football club and I won’t change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see.”

United’s next three league games are against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool.

Former captain Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: “It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That’s the problem the club have got.

“It is horrible to say that. I did think that last season that the club should have gone for the best manager they could have got and not given the job to Michael Carrick.

“Because I felt this might happen this quickly but this has gone very, very sour very quickly and the club is a mess.”

The Argentina legend has had a busy period of travel

articles.title: Alvarez strike sees Atletico pile pressure on Barcelona ahead of Clasico
articles.summary: Alvarez scored for the second time in as many games.
articles.content:
Alvarez strike sees Atletico pile pressure on Barcelona ahead of Clasico

Alvarez scored for the second time in as many games.

Last Update:

Julian Alvarez scored his first home goal of the season as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 to move Diego Simeone’s men within two points of LaLiga leaders Barcelona.

Alvarez, who tried to force through a move to Barca in the summer, got off the mark for the campaign in midweek with a goal in the 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart.

And he followed that effort up with a simple finish at the Metropolitano that put the pressure on Barca ahead of their Clasico with Real Madrid on Sunday.

Alvarez turned home from Alejandro Grimaldo’s cross three minutes into the second half, his close-range effort proving decisive as Atletico made it eight wins from 10 to start their league season.

Georges Mikautadze scored a 96th-minute winner as Villarreal won 2-1 at neighbours Valencia.

Pepelu’s emphatic penalty gave Valencia the lead, which looked to have been doubled when Cesar Tarrega fired in after Villarreal failed to clear a corner.

However, that was ruled out for offside and Alexander Freeman then levelled by heading home Sergi Cardona’s cross.

The game looked to have turned back in Valencia’s favour as Pape Gueye was sent off for an elbow on Jose Gaya.

Yet the hosts were also reduced to 10 men when Harvey Elliott received two yellows in succession for dissent, and Villarreal claimed the derby spoils at the death as Alberto Moleiro’s excellent pass was collected by Mikautadze, who emphatically converted to leave Valencia with just six points from 10 games.

Racing Santander beat Espanyol 2-1, and Elche were 3-0 winners at Rayo Vallecano.

Lazio go top, Roma stay unbeaten after thriller

Lazio moved top of Serie A with a 2-1 win over Parma as their city rivals Roma maintained their unbeaten start with a thrilling 3-3 draw at Napoli.

Gustav Isaksen had a first-half goal ruled out for offside for Lazio, but Kenneth Taylor’s effort and an own goal from Diego Carlos proved enough to secure the points.

They are three points ahead of defending champions Inter Milan in the Scudetto race ahead of the Nerazzurri’s clash with Fiorentina on Sunday.

Roma are four points off the pace but, like their arch rivals, are still yet to taste defeat after twice coming from behind to draw with Napoli.

Frank Anguissa’s stunning overhead kick put Napoli in front before their lead was doubled by Scott McTominay when he nodded in on the rebound after seeing an initial close-range header kept out.

But Matias Soule’s fine long-range strike saw Roma pull one back, with Leonardo Balerdi then lashing home a leveller from point-blank range.

McTominay restored Napoli’s lead with an unerring long-distance effort into the bottom-left corner, only for Balerdi to rescue a point by heading home his second.

Elsewhere, Como beat Sassuolo 2-0 and Bologna won at Cagliari by the same scoreline.

Dortmund return to summit

Borussia Dortmund moved back to the summit of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt.

Maximilian Beier was the difference as his 80th-minute goal secured the points, sending Dortmund three clear of Bayern Munich ahead of their meeting with third-placed Freiburg on Sunday.

Romulo Cardoso scored twice as RB Leipzig ran out 4-0 winners over Elversberg, while two penalties from Niklas Fullkrug helped Werder Bremen beat Mainz 3-2.

Paderborn were 1-0 winners over Hamburg, their victory seeing Union Berlin drop into the bottom two after a 1-1 draw at Augsburg in which both teams had a man sent off. Schalke drew 0-0 with Cologne.

In Ligue 1, Paris FC missed the chance to at least temporarily go top of the table as they were beaten 2-1 by Lens.

Florian Thauvin equalised for Lens after being teed up by Thorgan Hazard, with the roles then reversed as the latter fired home from Thauvin’s cross to complete the turnaround.

articles.title: De Zerbi labels Tottenham as ‘complete team’ after Spurs’ derby win at Chelsea
articles.summary: Spurs are up to 12th after successive wins.
articles.content:
De Zerbi labels Tottenham as ‘complete team’ after Spurs’ derby win at Chelsea

Spurs are up to 12th after successive wins.

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi hailed Tottenham as a “complete team” after they claimed a 2-0 London derby win over Chelsea.

Having gotten off the mark on Monday with their first Premier League win of the season over Coventry City, Tottenham prevailed away at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018, though they received a helping hand from Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders.

Penders, filling in for the injured Emiliano Martinez, endured a Premier League debut to forget as he punched a corner into his own net 13 minutes from the end of normal time.

Chelsea star Cole Palmer was then sent off for a second bookable offence, before Mathys Tel made sure of the points with a fine individual effort.

And De Zerbi was effusive in his praise of his players after they secured back-to-back wins to move up to 12th in the  table.

“It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also,” De Zerbi told Sky Sports.

“They deserved this win, they prepared very well. We are improving a lot, we are improving in the mentality, in the group and the relationships with the players and then we are improving on the pitch.

“Against Aston Villa, Everton for 30 minutes we were playing very well. Maybe no goals, no finishing good enough to score and maybe in the first bad moment we changed mentality. Now it is a complete team. The players are playing better, we improved in the style.

“When we stay for dinner and stay together in the dressing room I see a different group, a different relationship and different atmosphere among the players.

“The character was today great but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here last season, two or three seasons ago, they suffered the last results, two times 17th position, we are working to change the last part of the history of the club.

“We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room, many great players. I think if we work hard we can do something important.

“I have to believe for sure in this group. I never lost the confidence in my players. The week in Marbella [during the international break], to speak better face to face, to open ourselves and remove the mask it is important. It is important for the spirit, the belief. The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more important than the tactics.”

Chelsea came into the game on the back of successive victories, but head coach Xabi Alonso conceded the Blues were far below their best.

“We are all disappointed with the result, with the performance collectively and individually we were not at our best level,” Alonso told Sky.

“It was about the first goal and it went their way and with 10 men it was difficult but we can do better.

“Chances were the main thing, they had few and we had few. We spoke at half time we had to be patient and be mature. We can do better.

“We wanted to have this fluidity in the middle. We wanted the pockets filed with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. There were situations but overall we have to do better.”

articles.content:
Arteta calms Gabriel fears after Arsenal move level at top with Everton win

Gabriel recovered from an injury scare to secure the points for the Gunners.

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta allayed any fears of an injury to Arsenal centre-back Gabriel after he went down with a knee issue in their 2-0 win over Everton.

Arsenal moved level at the top of the Premier League table with Manchester City, who lost 2-1 at Aston Villa, as goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel secured the points for the defending champions, who made five changes from their draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League in midweek.

Gabriel doubled Arsenal’s lead in the 68th minute having earlier jarred his knee, the Brazilian heading home from Ben White’s cross.

And, with Arsenal set to face Liverpool next Sunday after an EFL Cup tie at Fleetwood Town, Arteta indicated the 28-year-old will likely be fine for the trip to Anfield.

“We all [thought he would have to come off] by the reaction of his team-mates,” Arteta told BBC Match of the Day.

“It was a really worrying action. We know Gabi and how tough and strong he is – and he seems to be OK.

“It’s a big win for us. It was a tough week with the schedule we had to go through, a lot of minutes and the games were coming thick and fast.

“We knew we had a very good opponent in front of us but, overall, we had a good performance and fully deserved to win.

“For the most part, I thought we were the better team and dominated the game.

“But Everton had their spells as usual. To be able to change five players and still play at that level is impressive.”

articles.title: Maresca remains upbeat despite City squandering unbeaten start
articles.summary: The Premier League leaders fell to a 2-1 defeat at Villa Park.
articles.content:
Maresca remains upbeat despite City squandering unbeaten start

The Premier League leaders fell to a 2-1 defeat at Villa Park.

Last Update:

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca appeared upbeat despite his side’s perfect start to the Premier League season coming to an end against Aston Villa.

City fell to a 2-1 defeat at Villa Park, with Nicolas Jackson scoring either side of an Erling Haaland header as the league leaders dropped points for the first time in the top-flight under Maresca.

Maresca insisted his side “didn’t deserve to lose” but admitted there are aspects of the game his players can improve on.

“I think the performance overall was good, the amount of chances that we created,” Maresca told TNT Sports.

“[In the] second half we just conceded the transition for the goal. Sometimes you have to defend a little bit better, a little bit more lucky in that transition. But it’s football.

“We’ll learn from that and we move on.”

‘There are things we can do better’

Maresca remained adamant that both of Villa’s goals were avoidable, but acknowledged that ruthlessness at both ends of the pitch was vital at the elite level.

“We also created many moments, many chances,” the City boss said.

“We played most of the game in their half. but you have to be clinical and you have to avoid mistakes.

“You can learn always from when you win and when you lose. For sure, there are things that we can do better.”

Next up for City is back-to-back games against high-flying Brighton. The first, on Wednesday in the EFL Cup at the Etihad, is followed three days later by another clash in Manchester, this time in the league.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany in ‘stable’ condition after training ground collapse – but recovery could take ‘weeks’
articles.summary: The 40-year-old was rushed to hospital on Friday.
articles.content:
Vincent Kompany in ‘stable’ condition after training ground collapse – but recovery could take ‘weeks’

The 40-year-old was rushed to hospital on Friday.

Last Update:

Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany is in a “stable” condition after collapsing at the team’s training ground, but recovery could take “weeks”, according to the club’s director of sport Max Eberl.

Kompany was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing at the club’s training ground. Initial reports indicated the 40-year-old was in a stable condition, but Eberl has now confirmed he has spoken with the Belgian.

“He will spend a few more days in hospital until everything is checked over,” Eberl said in a press conference on Saturday.

“It shows again how health is the most important thing in life – not football.”

Eberl said that the incident happened while Kompany, who has been dealing with a viral infection in recent days, was overseeing an U23’s training session.

The Bayern board member revealed that initial tests had “yielded some results”, but he insisted “further results are needed to determine exactly what it is”.

Eberl added: “Vinnie will get all the time. We’re not going to start setting any timeframes. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it’s a question of what the recovery time will be. We’re not talking in terms of days, but weeks.

“He’ll only come back when he’s fit.

“He’s in the best hands. The best thing we can do is support him emotionally with energy and love.”

Kompany had been in the dugout for Bayern’s 6-1 Bundesliga win over RB Leipzig last weekend but did not take part in any media commitments.

Kompany was also present for Bayern’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday despite his illness.

Bayern, who lead the Bundesliga on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, visit third-placed Freiburg on Sunday.

articles.title: Hansi Flick not after ‘catchy headlines’ as Barca boss refuses to be drawn into referee debate ahead of El Clasico
articles.summary: The first El Clasico of the season takes place on Sunday.
articles.content:
Hansi Flick not after ‘catchy headlines’ as Barca boss refuses to be drawn into referee debate ahead of El Clasico

The first El Clasico of the season takes place on Sunday.

Last Update:

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick refused to be drawn into the debate over referees ahead of the first El Clasico of the season on Sunday.

Flick’s side are currently top of LaLiga having won each of their opening nine matches, although they squandered their unbeaten record in the Champions League in midweek.

The Spanish champions lead their fierce rivals Real Madrid by six points ahead of the much-anticipated clash at the Camp Nou on Sunday.

Much of the pre-match debate has been around matters relating to referees, with the case over payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to the former vice-president of the Spanish referees’ committee (CTA) still ongoing.

However, Flick refused to comment on the issue, instead opting to focus on his team’s preparations.

Responding to a question about whether the row over the officials might impact the game, the Barcelona coach said: “It won’t have an effect. I trust the refereeing, and we are seeing a good level of officiating, and each one of us has to protect his players.

“I prefer to focus on preparing my team. This topic is linked to newspaper headlines, and I don’t want any catchy headline. All I want is to focus on my team.”

Flick expresses ‘great respect’ for Mourinho

Like his opposite number in the dugout, Jose Mourinho, who Flick said he has “great respect” for, the Barca boss spoke glowingly about the significance of Sundays fixture.

“El Clasico is different,” Flick said. “It’s the best game football has to offer, and everyone will be watching. The team is really looking forward to playing it.

“I have a good feeling. The players have recovered and are ready for the game.”

Expanding on his admiration for Mourinho, Flick added: “When someone manages teams at this level for many years, it reflects his quality, and he has proven that at all the clubs he has coached.”

Where to Watch Barcelona v Real Madrid: TV and online streams

Barcelona versus Real Madrid kicks off at 8pm GMT (9pm local time) on Sunday, October 25 at the Spotify Camp Nou.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho insists his Real Madrid team will win titles as he prepares for El Clasico return
articles.summary: The Real boss makes a return to El Clasico for the first time since 2013.
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho insists his Real Madrid team will win titles as he prepares for El Clasico return

The Real boss makes a return to El Clasico for the first time since 2013.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has insisted his Real Madrid side “will win titles” as he prepares for the first El Clasico of the season on Sunday.

Los Blancos travel to the Camp Nou trailing fierce rivals Barcelona by six points in LaLiga, with the hosts looking to maintain their perfect start to the league campaign.

Real’s fortunes, by comparison, has been somewhat less assured, having already lost twice in the league this season. However, they have preserved a 100% record in the Champions League – something Barcelona relinquished on Tuesday after a 4-2 defeat to holders Paris Saint-Germain.

And so with Real hungry to get their domestic season back on track, and Barca licking the wounds of a humbling in Europe, it makes for hugely intriguing clash on what will be Mourinho’s return to this fixture for the first time since 2013.

The Real boss, whose ties with Barcelona run deep having been a coach there 30 years ago under the late Sir Bobby Robson, did not mince his words when asked if Sunday’s game will be something of a litmus test of his side’s LaLiga credentials.

“No,” he said. “Mourinho’s Madrid will win titles.”

The 63-year-old, however, was less matter-of-fact in his assessment of Sunday’s fixture more widely, acknowledging the grandeur of the occasion.

“I think it’s a worldwide spectacle,” he said.

“There are other derbies around the world, but this is unique. Fans who love football stop to watch El Clasico.

“We’ve been playing well, winning matches and scoring goals. But a Clasico is different – the form book goes out the window. In my experience, the momentum you have going into the game does not mean much.”

READ MORE: Barcelona vs Real Madrid combined XI: Which club has the stronger squad?

Mourinho insists referee debate has ‘never bothered me’

The subject of referees has generated considerable debate ahead of the game, over the ongoing case pertaining to payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enríquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the Spanish referees’ committee (CTA).

It prompted Barca player Fermin Lopez to hit out at Mourinho’s continued criticism of officials, describing it as “tiresome”.

Mourinho responded by saying that Lopez “gets tired of our discourse” and insisted the subject of referees is not one that affects him.

“The referee’s name has never bothered me,” the Real boss said.

“I always start from the principle that the referee is good. It never bothers me to know if the referee is A, B, or C. What bothers me a little is when the rules are broken, which, according to internal information, have not been broken yet.”

“Three weeks ago, the name of one referee came out; this week, it’s another [Juan Martínez Munuera].

“Whoever it is, I hope it goes well for them.”

‘No big deal’

Understandably, Mourinho remained tight-lipped on the specifics of his game plan, but hailed Barca head coach Hansi Flick as a “great coach, doing an excellent job”.

However, the Real manager looked to play down the emotions of returning to the Camp Nou, adding: “It’s just like going to any other stadium.

“Obviously, we are talking about a team with a lot of quality. It’s not the same to play against a high-quality team as it is to play against a less strong one, but it’s no big deal.”

articles.title: Morgan Gibbs-White admits Nottingham Forest struggles are ‘not good enough’ as winless run continues
articles.summary: Morgan Gibbs-White says the wins are coming for Nottingham Forest.
articles.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White admits Nottingham Forest struggles are ‘not good enough’ as winless run continues

Morgan Gibbs-White says the wins are coming for Nottingham Forest.

Last Update:

Nottingham Forest captain Morgan Gibbs-White has admitted his side’s struggles in front of goal are “not good enough” after another frustrating Premier League outing.

Forest were unable to turn an encouraging performance into three points against Ipswich, with Gibbs-White convinced his team deserved more after dominating the second half.

The midfielder believes Forest are playing well enough to start winning matches but acknowledged that their inability to convert chances has become a major concern.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Gibbs-White insisted Forest’s recent performances have deserved better results.

“We have had so many good performances recently but never enough to get the three points and get over the line,” he said.

“I feel like we have had a lot of chances, the first-half was a mis-match, they were in control and then we were.

“The second-half, we were completely dominant and we should have won the game in my eyes. As long as we keep performing like this surely we have to win.

“This is a question we have been asking ourselves in training, we have been doing shooting drills and if you had seen how they were going in yesterday…But they just were not in the game.

“It is a topic of discussion and it is not good enough but I am proud of the boys for keeping going and performing high.”

Gibbs-White questions VAR involvement in Diop incident

Gibbs-White also addressed a controversial incident involving Issa Diop, who escaped a red card following a VAR review.

While the Forest midfielder agreed with the eventual decision, he questioned why the officials on the pitch had not been trusted to make the call themselves.

“My only question is, why did that have to go to VAR when both the referee and linesman are standing there watching, it should be an on-field decision there and then,” he said.

“I do agree with the decision because we don’t know if he was going to get there.

“I think there needs to be ownership on the pitch. The referee and the linesman could both see what could have happened but VAR always have to get involved. But it is what it is.”

articles.title: ‘It’s a privilege’ – Jaissle rejects talk of Newcastle pressure after back-to-back defeats
articles.summary: The Magpies head to Selhurst Park needing to stop the rot.
articles.content:
‘It’s a privilege’ – Jaissle rejects talk of Newcastle pressure after back-to-back defeats

The Magpies head to Selhurst Park needing to stop the rot.

Last Update:

Matthias Jaissle insisted managing Newcastle United is a privilege as he rejected talk of being under huge pressure following successive defeats.

Newcastle have struggled on their return to action following the international break, following up a 4-1 loss at Coventry City that saw them punished for failing to take first-half chances with a 1-0 home defeat to Aston Villa in which there was an absence of clear-cut goalscoring opportunities.

The Magpies sit 11th in the Premier League, three points above the relegation zone but just two adrift of the top six at this still early stage of the season.

However, ahead of Sunday’s trip to a Crystal Palace side just one point behind them in the table, Jaissle is in obvious need of a result, though he made it clear he is not feeling any additional strain because of recent poor results.

“I always said that it’s a privilege to be the coach of Newcastle United,” Jaissle told his pre-match press conference.

“I would not say that’s a huge pressure, I would use another word. It’s a great and a huge responsibility to take that job, to also lead them throughout the negative period. That was something we were aware of.

“There were already positive signs in the start of the season. Now there’s a setback at the moment, and you need to overcome that.

“The disappointment of the fans is a part of the game. They’re passionate, especially our supporters, but they’re great and then it’s also normal that they show the disappointment.

“This is normal in football, they have high expectations. They deserve to have these high expectations and we need to deliver.”

Newcastle forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo is a doubt due to illness, but winger Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey are both in contention to return to the squad following injury absences.

The Magpies have dealt with a significant number of injuries in the opening months of the season, their win over Hull City before the international break coming with nine first-team players unavailable.

And Jaissle, who took over in August following the departure of Eddie Howe in a summer that also saw former captain Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon depart, pointed to the limited time he has had to work with a full squad as a key reason why his players have yet to fully adapt to his style of play.

Asked how far away his team are from the vision of where he wants Newcastle to be, Jaissle replied: “We have for sure a lot of potential, I don’t want to name a percentage but there’s still quite a good gap to be refilled.

“I mentioned also a couple of days ago within the club to some decision-makers that sometimes we still feel in the pre-season when we train with the group now finally with almost every player on the pitch. That was not possible in the past weeks.

“We’re still implementing basics for our way of playing so it takes time, this is a process. The good part is that everyone within the club is realistic and can see that.”

articles.title: Unai Emery praises Enzo Maresca’s ‘fantastic job’ at Manchester City ahead of Aston Villa clash
articles.summary: Unai Emery has spoken ahead of Aston Villa's clash with Manchester City this weekend.
articles.content:
Unai Emery praises Enzo Maresca’s ‘fantastic job’ at Manchester City ahead of Aston Villa clash

Unai Emery has spoken ahead of Aston Villa's clash with Manchester City this weekend.

Last Update:

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has praised Enzo Maresca for the impact he has made at Manchester City, admitting his side face a difficult challenge against one of the Premier League’s strongest teams.

Villa host City on Saturday, with Emery’s side looking to close the gap on their opponents following a difficult start to the campaign.

The Spaniard believes Maresca’s understanding of City’s culture and playing style has been crucial to their impressive form, having previously worked under Pep Guardiola.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s fixture, Emery singled out Maresca as the driving force behind City’s performances.

“I think the key there is the coach. Enzo Maresca is doing a fantastic job,” Emery said.

“He worked with Guardiola, he worked in Leicester, successful, in Chelsea, successful.

“And now he knows Manchester City players – the culture, the club. And he is following the same way they did before with Guardiola. I think this is the key.

“They are favourite with Arsenal. The last year Manchester City and Arsenal they are so strong, so competitive in everything. The identity is clear. So we dream sometimes to be close to them.”

Aston Villa face Manzambi fitness concern ahead of City clash

Villa could be without summer signing Johan Manzambi for Saturday’s match, with the midfielder facing a late fitness test.

The in-form youngster has impressed since arriving at Villa Park, but his involvement against City remains uncertain.

Emery also confirmed that Amadou Onana, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Matteo Ruggeri will miss the fixture.

“Some players clearly out like Amadou Onana, Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Matteo Ruggeri,” he explained.

“Other players we will see how they are after the match we played on Wednesday and so on.

“They were with some pain, but I can’t tell you now until after the training session this afternoon.”

articles.title: Andoni Iraola insists Liverpool ‘need points wherever we can get them’ amid Anfield struggles
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola has spoken ahead of Liverpool's clash with Brighton on Sunday.
articles.content:
Andoni Iraola insists Liverpool ‘need points wherever we can get them’ amid Anfield struggles

Andoni Iraola has spoken ahead of Liverpool's clash with Brighton on Sunday.

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola insists his side must start collecting Premier League points regardless of where they play as he looks to secure his first home league win at Anfield.

The Reds have failed to win any of their opening three top flight matches at home under Iraola, although they have enjoyed better results at Anfield in other competitions.

Liverpool have beaten Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and Tottenham on home soil, with the Spaniard pointing to those performances as evidence that his players are capable of delivering in front of their own supporters.

Speaking ahead of Liverpool’s next Premier League fixture against Brighton, Iraola insisted he was more concerned about collecting points than ending a particular unwanted record.

“I want to win games. Home, away, we need points wherever we can get them,” he said.

“It’s true that the three games we haven’t won, but also our three games [wins in other competitions] have been high level games – Atletico, Villarreal, Spurs – and we won them with good performances at home also.

“We play at home the next two [Premier League] games so I would love to win them, but if we were playing away I would say the same.”

Iraola praises Liverpool youngsters and sends Ngumoha message

The Liverpool boss believes the progress of his young players has created a positive atmosphere, with each breakthrough encouraging others to follow.

“I think they are supporting each other. You could feel it straight away, even in pre-season and the ones who played the games,” Iraola said.

“You could feel after their performances they were looking at each other, praising each other and when they see one of them getting a start in the Champions League or in the Premier League and maybe it’s not themselves, but they feel it like ‘OK I am close to being there’.”

Ngumoha has attracted particular attention following his recent performances, including an impressive display against Villarreal in the Champions League.

However, Iraola urged the 18-year-old to remain focused on improving rather than becoming distracted by outside opinions.

“I think every player has to focus on performances – on keep doing well, improve the things they can improve,” he said.

“The outside noise, when it’s good, when it’s bad, I think it affects, obviously, but we have to not be affected by those things.

“Continue to do your job as good as you can, improve the things you can improve – don’t be affected by the things you hear.”

articles.title: Bayern boss Kompany rushed to hospital after training ground collapse
articles.summary: Kompany's condition is said to be stable.
articles.content:
Bayern boss Kompany rushed to hospital after training ground collapse

Kompany's condition is said to be stable.

Last Update:

Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was rushed to hospital after collapsing at the club’s training ground on Friday.

The former Manchester City and Belgium defender’s condition was reported to be stable, the 40-year-old having collapsed while watching Bayern’s reserve team train.

According to a report from Sky Sport Germany, an ambulance transported Kompany to hospital from Sabener Strasse, where a helicopter was reported to have landed in response to the incident.

A statement from Bayern read: “Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during an FC Bayern reserve team training session on Friday.

“The first-team head coach was watching the second string’s session. Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical care. His coaching staff will oversee training and match activities until further notice.”

Max Eberl, Bayern’s board member for sport, said: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure he makes a speedy recovery.

“Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs. His coaching team, in whom we have complete confidence, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.”

Kompany has been dealing with a viral infection that has forced him to miss several training sessions.

The 40-year-old was in the dugout for Bayern’s 6-1 Bundesliga win over RB Leipzig last weekend but did not take part in any media commitments.

Kompany was also present for Bayern’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday despite his illness.

Bayern, who lead the Bundesliga on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, visit third-placed Freiburg on Sunday.

articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi sends Chelsea warning as Tottenham boss looks to end Stamford Bridge curse
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi has warned Chelsea that Tottenham will not roll over on Saturday.
articles.content:
Roberto De Zerbi sends Chelsea warning as Tottenham boss looks to end Stamford Bridge curse

Roberto De Zerbi has warned Chelsea that Tottenham will not roll over on Saturday.

Last Update:

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi believes his side can overcome their miserable record at Stamford Bridge when they face Chelsea, insisting the club’s previous struggles should provide extra motivation.

Spurs have won just once in their last 34 league visits to Chelsea, making Stamford Bridge one of their most difficult away grounds.

However, De Zerbi is confident his players have the quality to change that record and has urged them to approach the London derby with belief and aggression.

Speaking ahead of the clash, De Zerbi acknowledged Tottenham’s poor record at Stamford Bridge but insisted he sees it as an opportunity rather than a burden.

“I think it’s not just this negative record, there are many, many negative records but for me it’s one motivation more and for the players,” he said.

“I want this negative record to give us more motivation and more mentality, more energy to win a game and play a good game because we have enough qualities to win this game.

“It’s against one very good team, very good coach and they have a clear style of play with great players,” De Zerbi added.

“But also the Tottenham players are very good, the level of the players is high. We have to show together as a team as well as individuals.”

Tottenham boss addresses discipline after Bentancur red card

De Zerbi was also questioned about Tottenham’s discipline following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending-off against Manchester United.

The midfielder was dismissed for a headbutt, raising concerns about how Spurs will handle the intensity of another heated Premier League encounter.

However, De Zerbi suggested he would rather see his players show too much emotion than approach matches without the necessary aggression.

“The balance is always difficult to fix – a balance between the energy, spirit, mentality,” he explained.

“If you have confidence in the players, you leave the players to decide their behaviour, to decide the reaction.”

“For sure, I prefer one ‘too strong’ reaction, than one player without blood, without reaction.”

articles.title: Chelsea boss Alonso compares Penders to Real Madrid goalkeeper Courtois
articles.summary: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has high hopes for Mike Penders, who will start in goal against Tottenham on Saturday
articles.content:
Chelsea boss Alonso compares Penders to Real Madrid goalkeeper Courtois

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has high hopes for Mike Penders, who will start in goal against Tottenham on Saturday

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso confirmed goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was facing a “few weeks” out after undergoing jaw surgery but says Chelsea are in safe hands with back-up Mike Penders, comparing him to Real Madrid great Thibaut Courtois.

Argentina international Martinez suffered a nasty injury at Everton last week after colliding with home defender Jarrad Branthwaite and has had an operation that means he will unavailable for the foreseeable future.

Alonso said: “Emi is doing better. He had the surgery and day by day he is feeling better, but we still need to wait. A few weeks. Hopefully, less than more, but we need to wait.

“The good thing is that he is feeling better and we need to listen to his feelings, the opinions of the doctors, the specialists, the surgeons. Considering it was a bad one, he is doing good.”

Chelsea boss Alonso draws Courtois comparisons

Penders replaced Martinez at the Hill Dickinson Stadium after 73 minutes and looked composed on his Chelsea debut.

There are high hopes for the Belgium stopper with Alonso admitting he reminds him of Courtois, the former Chelsea goalkeeper he worked with at the Santiago Bernabeu last season.

He said: “He’s ready. He’s been training well. He has shown he has a good level. When he came on, in a few minutes he showed his personality and qualities. That is why we have a squad to be ready for these situations.

“A lot of similarities [with Courtois]. Not just the nationality, but the stature. I spoke with Thibaut as well at the World Cup. He said himself he could see resemblances with Mike.”

Chelsea boss Alonso expecting tough test against Tottenham

Penders, who joined Chelsea from Genk in 2024 and spent last season on loan at Strasbourg, will start in goal on Saturday when Chelsea face Tottenham at Stamford Bridge.

The visitors enjoyed their first win of the Premier League season on Monday night, beating Coventry 3-1, and Alonso is wary of the threat posed by Roberto De Zerbi’s men.

He added: “Every derby is special. You feel the energy, the excitement from the stands. We need that energy to be used on the pitch. We need to have a good mentality for that and good emotional control. There’s a lot of passion from both sides.

“I have seen a good Spurs despite the results. We are expecting a tough game.”

Chelsea’s 2-0 victory at Everton moved them up to fourth in the Premier League table.

Malo Gusto missed the game on Merseyside and is fit to return but neither Pep Chavarria nor Emmanuel Emegha will be available.

“Malo is fine,” said Alonso. “Pep is training a little bit more, but he is not going to make it. Emmanuel is feeling better, but we need to wait.”

articles.title: PSG-Lyon rescheduled amid protests in Paris
articles.summary: The game is set to clash with the Ballon d'Or ceremony.
articles.content:
PSG-Lyon rescheduled amid protests in Paris

The game is set to clash with the Ballon d'Or ceremony.

Last Update:

Paris Saint-Germain‘s Ligue 1 game with Lyon has been rescheduled due to the unrest in Paris.

The game was originally scheduled to take place on Sunday at 8:45pm local time at the Parc des Princes.

However, it has now been moved to 8:30pm on Monday following a decree from the Paris Police Prefecture.

A statement from the French Professional Football League (LFP) read: “The LFP takes note of the police decree prohibiting the staging of the game between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais on Sunday at 8:45pm and has decided to reschedule the match for Monday at 8:30pm.”

The change will mean the game clashes with the Ballon d’Or ceremony, which is being held in London on Monday. PSG’s away game at Marseille last year was moved to a Monday due to storms, meaning it clashed with the Ballon d’Or ceremony in Paris, where the top prize was won by the capital club’s star forward Ousmane Dembele.

Police in Paris are moving resources elsewhere in preparation for another weekend of unrest in Paris and across France.

Violence broke out alongside protests over the cost of living last week, leading authorities to order partial curfews in Paris and other French cities.

Laurent Nunez, France’s interior minister, confirmed on Friday that around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed across France this weekend in anticipation of further violence.

Though the PSG game has been moved, the first NFL regular-season fixture to be staged in France will go ahead as planned.

The New Orleans Saints are set to face the Pittsburgh Steelers at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis in the northern outskirts of Paris. That game is scheduled to kick off at 2:30pm local time on Sunday.

articles.title: Saka set for MRI with severity of Arsenal winger’s injury ‘difficult to understand’ amid reports of eight-week absence
articles.summary: Arteta rejected claims Saka is burnt out but made it clear the workload has had an impact.
articles.content:
Saka set for MRI with severity of Arsenal winger’s injury ‘difficult to understand’ amid reports of eight-week absence

Arteta rejected claims Saka is burnt out but made it clear the workload has had an impact.

Last Update:

Arsenal still do not know the severity of Bukayo Saka’s injury, with Mikel Arteta revealing the winger is set for an MRI scan on Friday.

Saka was forced off during the first half of Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich on Wednesday.

The England forward played just 10 minutes at the Allianz Arena before limping off with an injury Arteta conceded “does not look good at all”. The BBC reported today the winger could be out for up to eight weeks.

Saka has a checkered injury history and his latest setback figures to serve as a significant blow to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining the Premier League title and challenging to lift the Champions League for the first time.

Speaking in a press conference ahead of Saturday’s meeting with Everton, Arteta said of Saka: “He’s going for an MRI this afternoon because he had a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the severity of the injury. We will know tomorrow.

“We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists, when a player is struggling to walk off the pitch and he’s restricted in his movement, they are not good signs.”

Player demands are intense – Arsenal boss Arteta

Asked if Saka is losing robustness, Arteta replied: “It’s been different in the last year or so, obviously the demands for ever player are immense, the intensity of those matches, the time between games is getting narrower, we played Sunday, then Wednesday and now Saturday, every hour is important.

“If they [the football authorities] can support the amount we are putting into these players, it would be really appreciated.

“We have to play three times in less than six games, the games are so demanding, we are chasing until the last minute.”

Arteta, though, rejected the suggestion Saka was suffering from burnout having helped England to third place in the World Cup in the summer and featured in three of the Three Lions’ UEFA Nations League matches during the recent international break.

“I don’t have that feeling at all,” Arteta said.

“Certainly what we have to be mindful of is creating the right ecosystem around a player to fulfil his qualities.”

articles.title: Passionate Carrick gives six-minute speech and admits Manchester United have lost their way but denies dressing room is divided
articles.summary: Michael Carrick appeared frustrated with Manchester United's current problems but vowed to work hard to get the club back on track
articles.content:
Passionate Carrick gives six-minute speech and admits Manchester United have lost their way but denies dressing room is divided

Michael Carrick appeared frustrated with Manchester United's current problems but vowed to work hard to get the club back on track

Last Update:

Michael Carrick spoke for six minutes at the start of Friday’s press conference, outlining the need for Manchester United to regain certain values he says are the club’s foundation.

Carrick’s side head into Sunday’s game against Bournemouth mired in their worst league start for 40 years and on the back of a woeful 4-1 drubbing at Como on Wednesday night.

The former United midfielder gave a passionate speech in front of the assembled media, and before any questions were asked, demanding a change of approach from everyone at the club.

He said: “I’ll start today. I just want to say a few things, really.

“Recently, we haven’t had a good time. I think that’s pretty obvious. So I totally accept what we’re going through at the moment.

“We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things I was seeing and that we were doing as a team. We haven’t done well enough lately. We’ve had a spell that we’re really not happy with.

“Wednesday was a bad night. It was a bad night for a lot of reasons. It hurt a lot. It obviously hurt me to see us play that way, to see how the game panned out. As I said after the game, it was really unacceptable.

“The supporters are a huge part of this football club. They have to make the effort and the time and money they spend, to feel how we all felt on Wednesday was a tough moment.”

We need to find Manchester United’s famous resilience – Carrick

Carrick cited the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Matt Busby, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney in demonstrating the kind of player that has made United one of the biggest clubs in the world. And he says they now have to tap into those values.

“The foundations of this football club and values have been etched down for many years,” he added.

“I totally understand and I get every single one of them. It comes down to being humble, to hard work and being really proud to live up to those values.

“There is a resilience about this football club that has been shown for a long, long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, sustaining success, there is a resilience to this football club that runs very, very deep.”

He added: “Manchester United always has been, and always will be, bigger than any single individual.

“Bigger than me, any of the players, it always has been. I’m fortune enough to know some players myself and played with some, Ryan Giggs is arguably one of the greatest to play for this football club. It was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United.

“Wayne Rooney is top goalscorer of this football club. His biggest thing was playing for the team, sacrificing for the team and what was good for Manchester United.

“Sir Alex Ferguson is the best manager of all-time. The greatest, for me. And working for him, his main priority was Manchester United. Going back to Sir Matt, Sir Bobby, the resilience was beyond belief in what they showed and the way they rebuilt this football club.

“Again it was based on being humble, having humility and hard work. We can never lose that and I won’t let us lose that.”

We’ve had conversations – United boss Carrick

Speculation about Carrick’s future has ramped up following the performance at Como with the likes of Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe linked with the post.

Brighton boss Hurzeler today distanced himself from the discussion while Conte also denied suggestions he has held talks with the Old Trafford heirarchy.

Carrick admitted there had been conversations internally and confirmed a reaction was now required, starting on Sunday.

He said: “We’ve spoken. There are always conversations going on. It’s pretty obvious how we’re all feeling. A reaction, a reaction from me.

“The responsibility for me in this position is to lead. It is my responsibility, whatever goes on the pitch and what we look like, what we feel like.

“I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet so everyone else can stay dry. That’s the position I’m in and it’s a privileged position.

“Discussions are going on, getting the players in a good frame of mind and well organised to put in a good performance on Sunday. 100% I can turn it round.”

Carrick dodges Fernandes captaincy question

Bruno Fernandes did little to aid Carrick on Wednesday night, blaming the United boss’ tactics for the defeat at Como. The Portugal midfielder is the second player to voice his opinion in recent weeks following Lisandro Martinez’s criticism of the club’s transfer window.

Martinez apologised but Carrick was not willing to speculate on whether Fernandes would have to do the same, or whether he would keep the captain’s armband at the weekend.

He said: “The most important thing is the team. I will always do what is best for the club. Whatever the situation is, I will always do what is best for the club.”

He also dismissed reports the dressing room was divided. “It’s not divided, no,” he said. “We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Conte denies ‘unfounded’ reports about Man United demands
articles.summary: Conte is seen as a top candidate should United part with Michael Carrick.
articles.content:
BREAKING: Conte denies ‘unfounded’ reports about Man United demands

Conte is seen as a top candidate should United part with Michael Carrick.

Last Update:

Antonio Conte has denied reports in Italy that he has given the green light to a move to a Manchester United on two conditions.

La Repubblica reported Conte had made two demands that would need to be met for him to commit to replacing the under-pressure Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

Conte was said to have insisted on full control over transfer strategy and the freedom to appoint a backroom staff of his choosing.

However, in a post on Instagram, Conte rejected those claims.

“Following recent media reports in Italy and abroad, I feel it is appropriate to clarify my position,” he wrote.

“My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage. Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.“I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my “strong personality”. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

“Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties’ needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.

“Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact.”

Carrick is under huge pressure following a dismal start to his first permanent season in charge of United.

The former Middlesbrough boss, who made 464 appearances for United and won 17 trophies with them as a player, enjoyed an excellent interim spell in charge last season, helping the Red Devils finish third and qualify for the Champions League.

But they have taken just six points from seven games to start the Premier League season, while they have already been knocked out of the EFL Cup.

Wednesday’s 4-1 defeat at Como made it two defeats from three in the Champions League, with Carrick’s position now thought to be hanging by a thread.

In addition to Conte, former Germany boss Julian Naglesmann has been linked with the job, while former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe is thought to be the preferred choice of director of football Jason Wilcox.

Conte left Napoli in May, having led them to Serie A glory in 2024-25.

A Premier League title winner with Chelsea, the former Juventus, Inter Milan and Italy boss last worked in England during an ill-fated spell with Tottenham, which came to an end in March 2023.

Meanwhile, Brighton and Hove Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler distanced himself from speculation linking him with the position.

“I’m really focused on my job here,” Hurzeler said ahead of Sunday’s game at Liverpool. “I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days and, beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and what he has done with Manchester United the last season.

“He’s a great human being, a great personality. There’s nothing more to say about that.

“I’m really privileged to be here,” Hurzeler said. “I’m part of a journey and I still have this feeling when I go to bed that we are not finished with our journey.

“I always emphasise that I’m not 100 per cent satisfied and happy with where we are, there are still improvements to make and potential to get out of the players.

“Therefore I really I want to work on that, together with my staff. I have a great group of players, players who support me and give everything for the club.

“We have built this [together] over the years. We’ve had good periods, we’ve had bad periods. To build these connections you need time. You don’t take these things for granted.

“It’s a people business. Making a people business out of this pressure business is something I don’t take for granted and something I won’t throw away that fast.”

United host Bournemouth on Sunday, which could be Carrick’s last chance to save his job.
