articles.title: Hurzeler distances himself from Manchester United job and says Carrick is a ‘great human being’
articles.summary: Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler was quick to shut down suggestions he'd be keen to join Manchester United should they sack Michael Carrick
articles.content:
Hurzeler distances himself from Manchester United job and says Carrick is a ‘great human being’

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler was quick to shut down suggestions he'd be keen to join Manchester United should they sack Michael Carrick

Last Update:

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler outlined his respect for Manchester United counterpart Michael Carrick, describing him as a “great human being”.

Hurzeler is reportedly on United’s shortlist should they decide to sack Carrick with United currently enduring their worst league start in 40 years.

The 4-1 hammering at Como in midweek was another major setback for United with captain Bruno Fernandes not helping Carrick’s cause by criticising his tactics after the game in Italy.

Despite the speculation around a potential move to Old Trafford, Hurzeler insisted his mind was firmly on matters at the Amex.

“I’m really focused on my job here,” he said ahead of Sunday’s game at Liverpool. “I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days and, beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and what he has done with Manchester United the last season.

“He’s a great human being, a great personality. There’s nothing more to say about that.”

I won’t throw Brighton job away – Hurzeler

Hurzeler joined Brighton from St Pauli in 2024 and in May signed a contract extension that ties him to the club until 2029.

“I’m really privileged to be here,” Hurzeler said. “I’m part of a journey and I still have this feeling when I go to bed that we are not finished with our journey.

“I always emphasise that I’m not 100 per cent satisfied and happy with where we are, there are still improvements to make and potential to get out of the players.

“Therefore I really I want to work on that, together with my staff. I have a great group of players, players who support me and give everything for the club.

“We have built this [together] over the years. We’ve had good periods, we’ve had bad periods. To build these connections you need time. You don’t take these things for granted.

“It’s a people business. Making a people business out of this pressure business is something I don’t take for granted and something I won’t throw away that fast.”

Hurzeler dismisses Brighton title challenge

Brighton head to Anfield in third place in the Premier League and on a run of four league wins without conceding, the latest of which saw them hammer M23 rivals Crystal Palace 5-0 last Sunday.

The Seagulls are two points behind second-placed Arsenal and five adrift of leaders Manchester City but Hurzeler dismissed talk of Brighton mounting a title challenge.

“No! We go game by game, we try to focus on performance,” he added.

“Just yesterday I had a conversation with the players and I love the way they are thinking. They said ‘we don’t want to focus on results, we want to focus on performances and how we get better, how we can improve because then the results will come’.

“Then we can speak at the end of the season about where we are, where we should have been. But now it is solution-focused, process-orientated and trying to get the best out of the players.”

articles.title: Achtung Julian! Kahn says Nagelsmann would be taking ‘enormous risk’ if he joins Manchester United
articles.summary: Legendary Germany goalkeeper Oliver Khan has warned Julian Nagelsmann off taking over at Manchester United if Michael Carrick is sacked
articles.content:
Achtung Julian! Kahn says Nagelsmann would be taking ‘enormous risk’ if he joins Manchester United

Legendary Germany goalkeeper Oliver Khan has warned Julian Nagelsmann off taking over at Manchester United if Michael Carrick is sacked

Last Update:

Former Bayern Munich and Germany goalkeeper Oliver Kahn says Julian Nagelsmann would be taking an “enormous risk” going to Manchester United where “every manager fails sooner or later”.

Nagelsmann is one of the leading candidates to take over should United dispense with Michael Carrick, who is on shaky ground with the club currently enduring their worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Wednesday night’s 4-1 hammering at Como in the Champions League was another awful result and performance with captain Bruno Fernandes not helping Carrick by questioning his manager’s tactics in the media afterwards.

Nagelsmann is believed to be on a shortlist that also includes Brighton’s Fabian Hurzeler, Aston Villa’s Unai Emery as well as Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe.

But Kahn, who worked as CEO at Bayern when Nagelsmann was head coach, believes the 39-year-old should consider a move to Old Trafford very carefully if he was offered the job.

He told German TV show Triple – der Hagedorn Fußballtalk: “From his point of view, it’s not an easy situation. He isn’t someone with a great deal of experience, particularly when it comes to foreign teams.

“He has to ask himself: What is my next step? Does it have to be the right one? Or do I immediately associate it with an enormous risk like Manchester United, where essentially every manager in recent years has failed sooner or later? You should look very carefully at where you’re going.”

Nagelsmann cannot afford another failure, says Kahn

Nagelsmann’s stock has fallen in recent years. After bursting onto the scene with impressive stints at Hoffenheim and RB Leipzig, his progress has stalled. A two-year spell at Bayern resulted in one Bundesliga title while with Germany he reached the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 and the round of 32 at the 2026 World Cup.

Kahn believes he needs to find a project that would enable him to get back on track.

He added: “Bayern Munich and the national team were already big blows for him. You have to think carefully: Where do my strengths lie? Which club can I really help? I think Julian is someone who can develop a club and a team and take them further. Whether Manchester United are the right next step for that is something only he can know.”

Howe and Conte are both out of work and would jump at the chance of taking over at United.

Nagelsmann is believed to be slightly more reticent while both Hurzeler and Emery are tied into contracts that would make it difficult, and hugely expansive, to extricate them from.

articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League: Dump Semenyo and Saka ahead of Gameweek Eight

Injuries largely dictate our list of the five players you should dump from your Fantasy Premier League squads ahead of Gameweek Eight

Last Update:

With another round of fixtures approaching, Fantasy Premier League managers have plenty of decisions to make. Injuries have hit several popular midfielders, while a couple of players who have started the season well might not offer the same value over the coming weeks. Here are five players I’d consider selling or avoiding ahead of Gameweek 8.

Antoine Semenyo

Price: 8.3mOwnership: 11.1%Position: MidfielderOpponent: AVL (A), BHA (H), NFO (A)

Semenyo is the easiest sell on this list, and not because his form has suddenly fallen away. The Manchester City winger damaged his knee against Ipswich last weekend and Enzo Maresca expects him to miss around eight weeks, putting a return somewhere near December. He has two goals and three assists this season, so there’s no doubting what he offers when fit. The problem is leaving 8.3m tied up in a player who won’t be helping your FPL side for the foreseeable future. City’s fixtures are still attractive, and Phil Foden or Rayan Cherki could offer a way back into their attack. I’d move Semenyo on.

Bukayo Saka

Price: 9.6mOwnership: 16.1%Position: MidfielderOpponent: EVE (H), LIV (A), HUL (H)

This one hurts, especially for anyone who brought Saka in for Arsenal’s good run. He lasted barely 10 minutes against Bayern Munich on Wednesday before going off with a quadriceps problem, and Mikel Arteta’s reaction afterwards wasn’t exactly reassuring. Everton at home would normally be a fixture to target, which is why I wouldn’t rush into a transfer before Friday’s press conference. But 9.6m is a lot to leave on the bench if the scans confirm a significant lay-off. Arsenal also visit Liverpool in Gameweek 9, so owners have a decision to make. Prepare a replacement now, but wait for the medical update.

Dominik Szoboszlai

Price: 6.8mOwnership: 18.8%Position: MidfielderOpponent: BHA (H), ARS (H), CRY (A)

Szoboszlai’s hamstring has become a proper headache for FPL managers. After missing matches earlier this month, he returned against Brentford and lasted just 32 minutes before the same problem flared up again. Liverpool are being cautious and he missed training ahead of Sunday’s Brighton match. At 6.8m, there’s little point keeping a midfielder if you’re not confident he’ll even make the squad, especially with Arsenal up next in the league. He could be back sooner than some feared, so there’s no need to invent a lengthy absence, but I’d rather use the transfer on somebody with dependable minutes. This feels a fairly straightforward sell.

Joško Gvardiol

Price: 5.8mOwnership: 28.1%Position: DefenderOpponent: AVL (A), BHA (H), NFO (A)

Gvardiol’s 41 points look respectable, but I’m not sure I’d be buying him at 5.8m right now. He has one goal and four assists, which has helped disguise the fact City have only kept two clean sheets so far. More worrying is the playing time: he’s managed 487 minutes out of a possible 630, and Enzo Maresca has enough defensive options to keep everyone guessing. Villa away isn’t the worst fixture, but Brighton follow and I’d rather pay for a defender I know will start. If you’ve got bigger injury issues, hold him. If you’re wildcarding or freeing up funds, he’s someone I’d consider moving on.

Pascal Groẞ

Price: 6.2mOwnership: 45.5%Position: MidfielderOpponent: LIV (A), MCI (A), BRE (H)

Groẞ has been brilliant for managers who started with him, so this isn’t about pretending his 58 points were a fluke. Three goals and four assists in seven matches is outstanding at 6.2m. The concern is whether that pace can last: his total expected goal involvements sit around three, well below the seven returns he’s already produced. Brighton also face Liverpool and Manchester City away in successive Gameweeks, a pretty nasty run to buy into. With Jack Hinshelwood back, there’s also the possibility Groẞ spends more time deeper, although that role change isn’t confirmed. I’d be wary of buying now and wouldn’t blame owners for banking the profit.

articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League: Foden heads list of five players you should target for Gameweek Eight

These five players will enhance your Fantasy Premier League team for the round eight games

Last Update:

Gameweek 8 in Fantasy Premier League is almost upon us, and there are a few interesting names worth looking at ahead of the weekend. Phil Foden might finally be finding his feet again at Manchester City, while some cheaper options are putting up numbers that deserve more attention. Here are five players I’d consider bringing in this week.

Alex Iwobi

Price: 5.4mOwnership: 1.1%Position: MidfielderOpponent: COV (A), AVL (A), NEW (H)

Fulham’s season hasn’t exactly taken off, but Iwobi is worth a look if you need a cheap midfielder. He finally scored against Hull last weekend and his involvement was hard to miss: four shots from close range and 12 successful passes into the opposition box. He’s also created six big chances this season, despite having no assists to show for it. That’s the sort of number that can turn into points quickly if his team-mates start finishing. Coventry away is up next, followed by Villa and Newcastle. At 5.4m and barely one per cent ownership, Iwobi could prove a handy differential rather than just another bench filler.

Bryan Mbeumo

Price: 7.8mOwnership: 20.5%Position: MidfielderOpponent: BOU (H), CHE (A), AVL (H)

There hasn’t been much to celebrate at Manchester United, but Mbeumo has quietly become a very decent FPL pick. Four goals and an assist in seven matches, with 4.84 expected goal involvements, isn’t the sort of output you can dismiss as luck. More importantly, he’s played every league minute and keeps getting shots away from dangerous positions. Bournemouth come to Old Trafford having struggled to shut teams out, which should suit his habit of drifting inside from the right. Chelsea away in Gameweek 9 is tougher, but Villa at home follows. At 7.8m, I’d rather buy his goal threat than pay a premium for Bruno Fernandes.

Phil Foden

Price: 6.8mOwnership: 1.9%Position: MidfielderOpponent: AVL (A), BHA (H), NFO (A)

Foden looks like one of those transfers that could be brilliant in a fortnight or leave you tearing your hair out over the team sheet. He scored against Ipswich last weekend, then followed it with a hat-trick against AEK Athens in midweek. Four goals in two games is a pretty convincing argument that his old form might be returning. At 6.8m and around two per cent ownership, the upside is obvious. Villa have allowed chances this season, while Brighton and Forest follow. Antoine Semenyo is injured but Rayan Cherki and Jeremy Doku mean minutes are still a worry, but after watching him find those pockets around the box again, I’m tempted to get in early for a Foden purple patch.

Liam Delap

Price: 5.5mOwnership: 1.9%Position: ForwardOpponent: IPS (A), BRE (A), MCI (H)

If you’re looking for a genuine one-week punt, Delap is worth a look. He returns to former club Ipswich on Friday with just one goal to his name this season, but his 18 shots are the most of any Nottingham Forest player. Ipswich have conceded 15 goals in seven matches, the most in the league, and are giving up plenty of big chances. Forest haven’t made the most of their opportunities either, which is why Delap remains a gamble rather than a safe buy. At 5.5m and under two per cent ownership, though, a goal at Portman Road could make a real difference. I’d view this strictly as a GW8 punt.

Evanilson

Price: 6.1mOwnership: 4.6%Position: ForwardOpponent: MUN (A), LEE (H), IPS (A)

Evanilson is starting to look a lot more useful than the average 6m forward. He’s got two goals and four assists from seven league starts, and has blanked only twice. Manchester United away might look awkward on paper, but Carrick’s side have struggled badly at the back and were beaten 4-1 by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. Bournemouth will fancy creating chances, particularly if they can get runners around Evanilson in the box. Leeds at home and Ipswich away follow, so there’s more to this than one fixture. He did start Thursday’s Europa League win over Milan, though, making the quick turnaround the obvious concern.

articles.title: Tchouameni opens up on clash with Real Madrid team-mate Valverde and admits it was ‘something ugly’
articles.summary: The clash between Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde rocked Real Madrid in May and the Frenchman has given his version of events
articles.content:
Tchouameni opens up on clash with Real Madrid team-mate Valverde and admits it was ‘something ugly’

The clash between Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde rocked Real Madrid in May and the Frenchman has given his version of events

Last Update:

Aurelien Tchouameni has spoken about his clash with Federico Valverde last season that caused ructions at Real Madrid, and insisted there was no fight but there was “something ugly”.

The France international and the Uruguayan clashed in a training ground incident in May that characterised a Madrid squad in turmoil under then boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

Valverde received hospital treatment for a cranioencephalic trauma, a form of concussion, and both men were fined €500,000.

Valverde insisted in a social media post that no punches had been thrown and Tchouameni backed up that version of events in an interview last night.

He told The Bridge: “People talk a lot, but there was no fight between Valverde and me. Yes, it’s true that things happen in the dressing room, but we never fought. In a dressing room there are arguments and things like that, but I never hit Valverde. It’s true, though, that there was something ugly.

“The only problem with all this is that it is Real Madrid and anything, no matter how small it is, gets very big and becomes a crazy media story. Something that wasn’t necessarily a problem, ends up being one.”

Valverde and I are closer now, says Real Madrid star Tchouameni

The incident caused a huge storm, especially as Madrid toiled on the field.

Tchouameni added: “Everyone called me to see what was going on and if I was okay. They want to know what happened, but nowadays you have to be very discreet. To calm people down I had to tell them that nothing was happening. I once saw an NFL documentary and there these things happen all the time.”

Both men insisted at the time that the row had been patched up and Tchouameni even claims it has brought them closer together.

“If you enter the dressing room today, as [coach Jose] Mourinho said, you will be able to see that Valverde and I are fine, there is no problem between the two of us,” he said. “On the field there is no problem either, life goes on. And in fact, these things bring you closer to the other person. We’re fine, we don’t have any problems.”

Madrid sit third in La Liga heading into Sunday’s El Clasico with leaders Barcelona at Camp Nou.

Europa League: Palace take point on the road while Celtic are beaten

Mateta's fine goal helps Eagles to much-needed point

Last Update:

Crystal Palace bounced back from their nightmare defeat at rivals Brighton last weekend with a fine 2-2 draw against Besiktas in the Europea League.

Two goals in four second-half minutes from Yeremy Pino and Jean-Philippe Mateta looked like giving the Eagles a win but Junior Olaitan levelled late on.

Celtic led Celta Vigo when Mika Baur steered in but then conceded a quick double as Celta Vigo came back to claim a win.

Juventus dropped their first points of ​the campaign after coming from behind to draw 2-2 with visitors Rennes.

Zeki Celik gave Juventus a fifth-minute lead, but the French side kept ⁠their composure and were level 10 minutes later when Jordan international Musa Al-Taamari finished from close range for his first goal in the competition.

Rennes then stunned the hosts with a Boulaye Dia penalty ⁠two minutes before the break ​as ⁠the Italians struggled to create chances until Nick Woltemade equalised from the spot in the 67th minute.

The German ⁠forward twice went close to scoring again as Luciano Spalletti’s ​team ⁠upped the pressure, and ‌Juve thought they had won it in the 88th minute when Jhon Lucumi found the net from close range, but ‌his effort was ruled out for offside.

Seagulls held

In the Conference League, a much-changed Brighton side were held to a tame 0-0 draw by Czech side Jablonec.

In his 100th game in charge Fabian Hurzeler saw a poor performance as Georginio Rutter wasted the best chances of the night.

Brighton are still unbeaten though and well placed on four points from their opening two games.

“We did not play on our highest level, Jablonec defended well,” Hurzeler said.

“Overall it’s not the result we wanted, but we have to keep going.

“If you play a 0-0 then you didn’t create enough, that’s definitely something we have to get better at.”

articles.title: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes to avoid punishment after Carrick criticism
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes will avoid punishment from Manchester United over his comments following their Champions League defeat to Como.
articles.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes to avoid punishment after Carrick criticism

Bruno Fernandes will avoid punishment from Manchester United over his comments following their Champions League defeat to Como.

Last Update:

Manchester United have decided not to punish Bruno Fernandes following his public criticism of Michael Carrick after Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como.

The United captain questioned Carrick’s tactical approach following the loss in Italy, suggesting it was the responsibility of the manager and his coaching staff to identify problems and make changes during matches.

Despite concerns over his comments, Fernandes will retain the captaincy and will not face disciplinary action.

The decision comes amid growing unrest at Old Trafford, with former United striker Wayne Rooney launching a scathing attack on the club’s players.

The Portuguese midfielder conducted 10 post-match interviews despite being substituted for Joshua Zirkzee midway through the second half.

However, the club have decided against taking disciplinary action.

It remains unclear whether Fernandes will start Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Rooney slams United players as ‘selfish’ and ‘like babies’

Former United captain Rooney was furious with the performance against Como and accused the players of attempting to shift responsibility away from themselves.

“When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart,” Rooney told the United Stand podcast.

“That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because they don’t want to take responsibility.”

Rooney insisted Fernandes and his teammates needed to take greater accountability for their performances.

“These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

“If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.

“He [Fernandes] is putting pressure on someone else because he doesn’t want to face it,” Rooney added.

“If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez and all of them looked at themselves in the mirror, they’ll find what’s looking back at them is them, and that’s not good enough. They need to show more.”

articles.title: Jose Mourinho defends Vinicius Junior after Real Madrid fans turn on Brazilian star
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has encouraged Vinicius Junior to keep working to restore his form for Real Madrid.
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho defends Vinicius Junior after Real Madrid fans turn on Brazilian star

Jose Mourinho has encouraged Vinicius Junior to keep working to restore his form for Real Madrid.

Last Update:

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has defended Vinicius Junior after the Brazilian was booed by his own supporters during Wednesday’s 4-1 Champions League win over RB Leipzig.

Vinicius has endured a difficult start to the season, scoring just once in 11 appearances, and was again unable to find the net at the Santiago Bernabeu.

The 26-year-old was substituted in the 70th minute, with sections of the home crowd making their frustration clear.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho admitted that criticism from home supporters can be particularly difficult for players to handle.

“When you are on the pitch and you are whistled when playing away, often it’s a boost to your motivation. When it’s at home, it hurts,” he said.

“Only he can say whether he feels sad, but I am pleased.

“Vini put in a good tactical performance. Vini defended very well. He then had a chance to score a brilliant goal, but the goalkeeper made a great save.

“Work, work. He cannot play but he can work his physique with an individualised plan,” he told TNT Sports Brazil.

“But I was happy with his performance. Ok, he didn’t score, he wasn’t man of the match but he had a good game for the team.”

Mbappe urges Vinicius to stay confident

Mbappe also offered his support after another frustrating evening for his attacking team-mate.

The Frenchman was named player of the match after assisting Madrid’s second goal and scoring their third.

Despite Vinicius’ struggles, Mbappe believes his frustration demonstrates how much he cares about performing for the club.

“He’s doing well,” Mbappe said.

“It’s good that he’s upset because it means he wants to give a lot to the team and the fans.

“I think he just needs to stay calm and proud of who he is. A great player must always take pride in who they are and gain confidence because the quality is there.”

Vinicius appeared to acknowledge his difficult situation on social media after the game, writing: “Living in the moment. Everything passes.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi receives incredible reception in Spain ahead of award ceremony
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has been greeted by dozens of fans in Oviedo ahead of receiving an award for sports.
articles.content:
Lionel Messi receives incredible reception in Spain ahead of award ceremony

Lionel Messi has been greeted by dozens of fans in Oviedo ahead of receiving an award for sports.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi was greeted by hundreds of supporters as he arrived in Oviedo on Thursday to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports.

The Argentina legend travelled from the United States to northern Spain for the prestigious ceremony, which will take place at the Campoamor Theatre on Friday afternoon.

Messi, who was accompanied by his wife Antonela Roccuzzo and personal assistant Pepe Costa, was met by huge crowds outside the Hotel de la Reconquista.

Supporters had gathered from early in the morning hoping to catch a glimpse of the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, with his arrival sparking celebrations in the Spanish city.

Messi arrived in Oviedo at approximately 10:15am local time, where he was welcomed by Ana Isabel Fernandez, president of the Princess of Asturias Foundation.

The 39-year-old received a traditional Asturian welcome, complete with bagpipes, as supporters cheered his arrival.

After entering the hotel, Messi later returned outside alongside Fernandez to acknowledge the crowds who had waited to see him.

Despite the security presence, the former Barcelona forward took time to greet supporters and sign autographs.

The Argentine remains an enormously popular figure in Spain following his remarkable career at Barcelona, where he established himself as one of football’s greatest players.

Messi to receive Princess of Asturias Award for Sports

Messi has been selected as the 2026 recipient of the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, recognising his extraordinary achievements and contribution to football.

The ceremony will take place at Oviedo’s Campoamor Theatre on Friday afternoon, with the Inter Miami forward expected to be among the main attractions.

His stay in Asturias will last less than 48 hours, but he has several engagements scheduled during his visit.

On Thursday afternoon, Messi is due to attend an event involving students and members of the region’s academic community.

Around 3,000 young people have been selected to participate after organisers received nearly 20,000 applications.

articles.title: Erik ten Hag suggests Cristiano Ronaldo is ‘holding his country captive’ in scathing interview
articles.summary: Erik ten Hag has once more launched an attack on Cristiano Ronaldo.
articles.content:
Erik ten Hag suggests Cristiano Ronaldo is ‘holding his country captive’ in scathing interview

Erik ten Hag has once more launched an attack on Cristiano Ronaldo.

Last Update:

Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has launched a fresh attack on Cristiano Ronaldo, accusing the Portugal captain of putting his personal brand ahead of his country’s interests.

Ten Hag, who endured a difficult relationship with Ronaldo during their time together at Old Trafford, believes the 41-year-old is preventing Portugal from reaching their full potential.

The Dutchman, now technical director at FC Twente, also questioned whether Ronaldo remains capable of competing at the highest level.

Speaking in an interview with Dutch publication Voetbal International, Ten Hag suggested Ronaldo’s priorities have shifted away from achieving success with his team-mates.

“Cristiano Ronaldo acts as if he were bigger than the club and country he plays for. It’s not about the team,” he said.

“It’s about his brand. Maximizing his profits, that’s what he’s all about.

“Now he’s holding his country captive. A whole crop. While Portugal has a great team, without him things turn better.”

Ten Hag claims Ronaldo can no longer compete at the highest level

Ten Hag also questioned whether players of Ronaldo’s age can continue performin against elite opposition.

“At country level, older players can still play a role. At club level, in the Champions League, you don’t see this anymore,” he said.

“35, 36 years; then it’s just over. With some exceptions. But nature catches up with everyone. Also Cristiano Ronaldo.”

Despite his criticism, Ten Hag insisted he was not attempting to diminish Ronaldo’s extraordinary achievements throughout his career.

“He was a great footballer, of course, that’s beyond dispute. But it’s not him anymore.

“I don’t want to be right, but it’s clear: he won’t win anything appealing with his team anymore.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Michael Carrick to remain in charge of Manchester United for Sunday’s game with Bournemouth
articles.summary: Michael Carrick will address the media as usual on Friday lunchtime, indicating he will be in charge of Manchester United for the weekend clash with Bournemouth
articles.content:
BREAKING: Michael Carrick to remain in charge of Manchester United for Sunday’s game with Bournemouth

Michael Carrick will address the media as usual on Friday lunchtime, indicating he will be in charge of Manchester United for the weekend clash with Bournemouth

Last Update:

Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for Sunday’s game with Bournemouth.

There has been an element of uncertainty around his position following last night’s Champions League thumping by Como but United confirmed this afternoon that Carrick will speak to the media on Friday at 1.30pm at his usual pre-match press conference.

If United were thinking of a change prior to the weekend, it is highly unlikely the former Middlesbrough boss would be put up to speak.

Carrick has presided over United’s worst league start in 40 years with his side winning just one of their opening seven games. And his position was weakened further after the Como game with captain Bruno Fernandes questioning his tactics.

Fernandes told TNT Sports: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence.”

Asked whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: “That’s on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.”

Carrick was uncharacteristically blunt when asked later about Fernandes’ remarks, saying: “There’s a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you aren’t going to win.”

Sympathy for Carrick from United board

There is reportedly an element of sympathy for Carrick’s position among the United hierarchy although the BBC today suggested replacements are already being identified.

The problem is the potential successors are not particularly inspiring while the United board also accept their role in what was an underwhelming summer window which left the squad with just one specialist left-back and no back-up for number nine Benjamin Sesko.

Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann are all out of work and would jump at the chance of taking over at Old Trafford. Other potential targets, Unai Emery and Fabian Hurzeler are under contract at Aston Villa and Brighton respectively, and it would require significant compensation to lure them away.

United have a nasty run of fixtures coming up, starting this weekend against a Bournemouth side whose athleticism could cause Carrick’s men problems. Their league fixtures after that are against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool.

articles.title: Harry Kane wants to know Ballon d’Or result early as Bayern Munich star closes in on historic award
articles.summary: Harry Kane has opened up on potentially winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday.
articles.content:
Harry Kane wants to know Ballon d’Or result early as Bayern Munich star closes in on historic award

Harry Kane has opened up on potentially winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday.

Last Update:

Harry Kane has admitted he would prefer to know whether he has won the Ballon d’Or before Monday’s ceremony, with the Bayern Munich striker among the leading contenders for football’s biggest individual prize.

The England captain is the bookmakers’ favourite to claim the award following another remarkable year in Germany, although Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal is also in contention.

Kane, 33, could become the first English player to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

However, he insists he has received no indication of the result and will have to wait until the ceremony to discover whether he has won.

Speaking after Bayern’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal on Wednesday, Kane opened up on the award.

“They want everyone to go, all the big names there and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know, so I can understand why,” he said.

“From my point of view, of course, I’d love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night.

“But it is their decision, I can’t control that. We’ll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.

“I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to,” he added.

“There are always rum ours flying around and you try to stay away from it.

“Of course I am going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It is a big occasion so we will have to wait and see.”

Kane closes in on Champions League record

Kane strengthened his Ballon d’Or credentials by scoring against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, extending his remarkable Champions League scoring streak.

The striker has now found the net in 10 consecutive matches in the competition, leaving him just one game short of Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of 11.

However, Bayern were unable to secure all three points against the Gunners, with the 2-2 draw leaving them 14th in the Champions League league phase after three matches.

Vincent Kompany’s side have collected five points from their opening three European fixtures, recording one win and two draws.

Attention now turns to Sunday’s Bundesliga meeting with Freiburg, where Bayern will look to maintain their position at the top of the table.

articles.title: Barcelona official slams Real Madrid as ‘a disgrace’ and launches attack on Jose Mourinho ahead of Clasico
articles.summary: Barcelona meet Real Madrid in El Clasico this weekend.
articles.content:
Barcelona official slams Real Madrid as ‘a disgrace’ and launches attack on Jose Mourinho ahead of Clasico

Barcelona meet Real Madrid in El Clasico this weekend.

Last Update:

Barcelona president Joan Laporta’s advisor Enric Masip has launched a furious attack on Real Madrid and Jose Mourinho ahead of Sunday’s Clasico, accusing their rivals of damaging Spanish football.

Masip, who serves as an advisor to Laporta, criticised Madrid’s conduct amid the ongoing tensions between the two clubs surrounding the Negreira case.

Speaking at the Nacex Challenge event at Club Golf Barcelona, the former handball player also took aim at Mourinho, contrasting the Real Madrid manager’s behaviour with that of Barcelona boss Hansi Flick.

“What Madrid does is a shame and is mistreating the entire competition,” he said.

“When someone uses these techniques, they advance to cover up their own problems by referring to their greatest rival.

“In three and a half years, nothing has ever been proven and will never be done. There has been nothing.

“It has been years since we alluded to dark times in this country when a team did benefit and won titles because of that impartiality. Red lines have been crossed.”

Mourinho targeted ahead of Sunday’s Clasico

Masip reserved some of his strongest criticism for Mourinho, who is preparing to face Barcelona at Camp Nou this weekend.

The advisor referenced Mourinho’s infamous confrontation with former Barcelona assistant Tito Vilanova, when the Portuguese coach poked him in the eye during a heated Clasico in 2011.

“When someone says they see strange things… strange things is putting your finger on a coach,” Masip said.

“He (Mourinho) throws darts. Watch a press conference Mourinho and one of Flick… Flick, they are the values of the Barca.”

Masip added: “For Mourinho and Real Madrid the other person is always to blame.”

articles.title: Haaland is 100% fit, says Manchester City boss Maresca, who also defends Cherki showboating
articles.summary: Manchester City will be at full strength for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa after resting some key players - including Erling Haaland - for the midweek win over AEK Athens
articles.content:
Haaland is 100% fit, says Manchester City boss Maresca, who also defends Cherki showboating

Manchester City will be at full strength for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa after resting some key players - including Erling Haaland - for the midweek win over AEK Athens

Last Update:

Erling Haaland is “100%” available for Manchester City’s trip to Aston Villa on Saturday.

The Norway striker was rested for the midweek Champions League win over AEK Athens, remaining on the bench for the duration, but will lead the line at Villa Park in the lunchtime kick-off.

Asked for an update on the fitness of Matheus Nunes, Nico O’Reilly, Mateo Kovacic and Haaland, City boss Enzo Maresca said: “We have a session this afternoon. They can be all available or not. Yesterday they were all improving, and we’ll see this afternoon.

“Erling is the only one 100% available, and the other three we need to wait for today’s session.”

I know how good Foden is, says City boss Maresca

Haaland, who is the Premier League’s top scorer with eight goals in seven appearances this season, is likely to link-up with Phil Foden at the weekend with the England midfielder the inspiration behind the win over AEK with a hat-trick.

Foden has had a difficult couple of years with niggling injuries and some indifferent form but Maresca is hoping he will return to his best.

He added: “I sat with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning. Just to show, I don’t know if ‘love’ is the right word to use, how important he is. I know Phil from years ago, so I know how good he is.

“For different reasons in the last years he was not good enough, but when you have more players like Phil available, you’re a better team. It’s a matter of improving players – if you improve the players, you improve the team. So, for me, I think it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England.”

Villa may have to contend with a front three of Haaland, Foden and Rayan Cherki after Maresca confirmed all three could play together “depending on the gameplan”.

Cherki has been another instrumental player in City’s strong start that has seen them win each of their first seven Premier League  games. The former Lyon playmaker has four goals and two assists despite seemingly driving Maresca mad.

“At this moment, is one of the best players in Europe,” said Maresca. “When he’s in the right position, that means when we’re able to find him between the lines, it’s always dangerous. And when he’s inside the box with the quality he has… He’s one of the best players in Europe.

“Sometimes because he loves the ball and loves to move a lot, most of the time he’s out of position. But when he’s in the right position, he’s always a weapon for us.”

Maresca defends City star Cherki after showboating criticism

Cherki received some criticism in midweek for showboating against AEK but Maresca didn’t have a problem with it.

“I like players when they’re happy, for sure, 100%,” he said. “But I also like simple things. At the end, I think the most difficult thing in football is to do the easy things, don’t complicate.

“But sometimes you have players that are so, so good like Rayan, that they need to do that. So I’m very happy when he’s doing that, also because I know that he’s happy. And if you’re able to do that and to allow the team to create chances, it’s top, it’s even better.”

City will head to the Midlands in confident mood but Maresca is wary of a Villa side that have picked up in recent weeks after a slow start.

He added: ”I have huge respect for Unai [Emery]; he’s done well in all clubs he’s been. He’s a fantastic manager, they’re a very good team, you can recognise the team, see clearly what they want – very intense off the ball. They are also, in this moment, in a good mood, winning games. I have respect for Unai and I’m 100% sure that it’s going to be a very tough game.”

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes is a ‘disgrace’ and is ‘killing Manchester United’, according to Jamie Carragher
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has blasted Bruno Fernandes after the Manchester United skipper questioned boss Michael Carrick's tactics following the 4-1 defeat at Como last night
articles.content:
Bruno Fernandes is a ‘disgrace’ and is ‘killing Manchester United’, according to Jamie Carragher

Jamie Carragher has blasted Bruno Fernandes after the Manchester United skipper questioned boss Michael Carrick's tactics following the 4-1 defeat at Como last night

Last Update:

Jamie Carragher has lashed out at Bruno Fernandes, describing him as a “disgrace” and accused him of “killing” Manchester United.

Fernandes’ attitude has been called into question following last night’s 4-1 Champions League hammering at Como after which the Portugal international suggested he felt boss Michael Carrick’s tactics had been a contributing factor.

United captain Fernandes told TNT Sports: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence. That’s on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.”

United captain Fernandes is like a kid in the schoolyard – Carragher

Carragher, who made over 700 appearances for United’s arch rivals Liverpool, told CBS Sports: “For Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really.

“When you think about last season, he got player of the year. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. He wouldn’t have got that award without Michael Carrick, because Michael Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he’s a talented footballer.

“But when you think of him as a footballer, he’s a talent, but in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it’s not right at all.

“And he’s reacted like that because he’s been brought off and he’s been embarrassed tonight by the manager as he brought him off. And when he talks about pressing, whether it’s man to man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can’t press because he does things for the crowd.

“I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he’s working hard – he’s not. He’s killing the rest of the team doing it.”

Fernandes is not captaincy material, according to the TV pundit, who added: “Years ago, there was a captain called Bryan Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man United because he played for the club, he didn’t throw the manager or the players under the bus.

“He kept fighting for Manchester United and watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace, calling the manager out considering how he’s performed this season on the pitch.

“Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be.”

Manchester United is rotten from top to bottom, says Carragher

Carrick’s job is now under serious threat, although the list of potential replacements is hardly stellar, and it remains to be seen if he is still in post when United play again, against Bournemouth on Sunday.

But Carragher believes the blame for United’s current predicament should be directed elsewhere.

“Isn’t it funny?” he said. “How many managers has he had, Bruno Fernandes? So every single manager at Manchester United doesn’t have an identity? How many managers are we on now for Bruno Fernandes? Five? They change the manager every season… Manchester United is rotten from top to bottom.

“I said earlier on, it’s not about the manager. It’s everything about the club. And who has got the answers? We comment on it all the time, ‘they might need to change the manager or do this, do that.’ Are we ever right really? Because no one ever seems to get it right. But listen, there’s no doubt the manager needs to be changed now. Right now this can’t go on for a club of the stature of Manchester United.

“But I’m glad Michael Carrick come out and just said that about Bruno Fernandes, that he don’t run, because they don’t run, this team.

“I’m delighted he brought him off, Fernandes, and I’m delighted that he had a little pop back there in the press because that’s what they need some of those players.”

articles.title: Manchester United: Howe leads uninspiring managerial contenders for Old Trafford post
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's time at Manchester United is likely to come to an end over the next few weeks but who are the candidates to replace him at Old Trafford?
articles.content:
Manchester United: Howe leads uninspiring managerial contenders for Old Trafford post

Michael Carrick's time at Manchester United is likely to come to an end over the next few weeks but who are the candidates to replace him at Old Trafford?

Last Update:

The writing is on the wall for Michael Carrick.

If the manner of Manchester United’s 4-1 hammering at Como in the Champions League was not alarming enough, the obvious split between head coach and captain afterwards demonstrated a power struggle that will only end one way.

Bruno Fernandes’ criticism of the tactics employed by Carrick in Italy showed there is a lack of respect for the former England midfielder in the dressing room. Fernandes had no qualms about calling out his boss with his remarks coming just a week after Lisandro Martinez also fired barbs at the club’s technical director Jason Wilcox.

Asked to describe what went wrong against Como, the Portuguese midfielder told TNT Sports: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence.”

Asked whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: “That’s on the manager and staff to see it, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.”

Carrick was uncharacteristically blunt when asked later about Fernandes’ remarks, saying: “There’s a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you aren’t going to win.”

Fernandes was hauled off after 67 minutes at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia after a display low on energy but high on arm waving.

It now remains to be seen whether Carrick will remain in post prior to Sunday’s home game with Bournemouth. If he does, it will be interesting to see the reaction from the Old Trafford crowd to Fernandes.

The former Sporting CP midfielder is supremely gifted, as evidenced by his winning of the PFA Player of the Year award last season, but the suspicion has always been he quickly becomes a negative influence when things start to go wrong.

It can’t be a coincidence that he, and the likes of Harry Maguire, continue to linger at United despite the frequent changes in the dug out.

So, what if Carrick is fired? Who are the contenders?

Eddie HoweStill regarded as a success at Newcastle despite spending close to £1billion during his five-year stint at St James’ Park. For that hefty outlay, Howe managed to win one trophy, the 2025 EFL Cup. His style of play, aggressive against lesser sides but passive against the big guns, may not sit easy with the United faithful.

Antonio ConteA serial winner after claiming the Scudetto with Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli. Also won the Premier League crown with Chelsea in 2017. The downside is the Italian’s combustible nature and whether that would work in United’s current set-up.

Fabian HurzelerHurzeler has come into the equation due to Brighton’s current form. The 33-year-old has done a fine job at the Amex, guiding the Seagulls to third in the Premier League table. Has just four years’ managerial experience under his belt and has benefited from the excellent recruitment programme at Brighton. He would not get that at Old Trafford.

Julian NagelsmannAnother relatively young manager at 39, Nagelsmann burst onto the scene with impressive stints at Hoffenheim and RB Leipzig. Since then, though, his progress has stalled. A two-year spell at Bayern Munich resulted in one Bundesliga title while with Germany he reached the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 and the round of 32 at the 2026 World Cup.

What’s next for Manchester United

The fixtures do not look kind for United with some tricky games coming up over the next month.

Tip of the Day: More European woe for Celtic

Celtic have struggled in Europe this season and our Tip of the Day predicts more misery for Martin O'Neill's men

Last Update:

The Europa League and the Conference League take centre stage tonight and we have identified two teams we fancy in Thursday’s Tip of the Day.

First up, we have Celta Vigo. The Liga side visit a Celtic outfit that enjoyed a resounding win over Hearts at the weekend to again demonstrate their strength domestically but they are struggling to make the step up to continental competition.

Martin O’Neill’s men exited the Champions League in the qualifiers, squandering a 3-0 first-leg advantage to LASK Linz, losing the second leg 5-1 in Austria.

They haven’t found the Europa League any easier, a 3-1 defeat at home to Ferencvaros followed by a 4-1 pummelling at Benfica.

Tonight, they host a Celta Vigo side who are also pointless in Europe’s second tier competition but sit eighth in the Spanish top flight and are unbeaten in six domestic games.

Our second tip is for AZ Alkmaar to win at Ararat Armenia.

AZ were unfortunate to lose 1-0 at Sunderland in their Europa League opener but bounced back with a 2-1 victory over Hapoel Beer Sheva.

They are going well in the Eredivisie, sitting second, and ought to be too good for a team that has yet to win in the competition, suffering convincing defeats to Sparta Prague and Jagiellonia.

articles.title: Declan Rice names Harry Kane as ‘clear winner’ of Ballon d’Or as Arsenal star hails battle in Champions League.
articles.summary: Declan Rice had nothing but praise for Harry Kane after Arsenal met Bayern Munich in the Champions League.
articles.content:
Declan Rice names Harry Kane as ‘clear winner’ of Ballon d’Or as Arsenal star hails battle in Champions League.

Declan Rice had nothing but praise for Harry Kane after Arsenal met Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Last Update:

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice believes Harry Kane should win the Ballon d’Or, describing the England captain’s performances over the past year as “remarkable”.

Rice praised his international team-mate after Arsenal’s Champions League clash with Bayern Munich, insisting Kane’s goalscoring numbers and overall quality make him the standout candidate for the award.

Speaking to TNT Sports, Rice made his feelings clear when asked whether Kane deserves to be recognised as the world’s best player.

“He is the clear winner,” Rice said.

“His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.

“He is ridiculous, such a good player and I am lucky I can play with him, not so lucky I have to play against him.”

Rice explains Arsenal goal against Bayern Munich

Rice also discussed his own performance, revealing how Arsenal’s tactical approach helped him find space against Bayern’s man-to-man marking system.

“When you play against teams who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles,” he explained.

“They follow you all over the pitch but I lost my man and I just kept running and lot my runner and then I was in on the goal. So happy.”

The midfielder reserved particular praise for Gyokeres, whose movement helped create the opportunity for Rice to score.

“Gyokeres has been making such a good impact coming off the bench. He made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal.”

Rice believes Arsenal’s willingness to attack Bayern on their own ground reflects the mentality Mikel Arteta has instilled in the squad.

“It is what the manager has drilled into us. We aren’t just going to come here and sit,” he added.

“At home they are probably one of the best teams in Europe so to come here tonight and give that account of ourselves was really good. We have to keep going.”

articles.title: Champions League: 10-man Inter finally get off the mark
articles.summary: The Serie A champions prevailed despite a second-half red card.
articles.content:
Champions League: 10-man Inter finally get off the mark

The Serie A champions prevailed despite a second-half red card.

Last Update:

Champions League headlines

Como pile pressure on Carrick with Man United thrashing

Rice rescues point for Arsenal against Bayern

Diomande scores against Leipzig as Madrid win fourth straight before Clasico

Villa make it three from three against Viking

Inter off the mark at third time of asking

Inter Milan claimed their first Champions League win of the season by beating Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 at San Siro despite Alessandro Bastoni’s red card.

The Nerazzurri were reduced to 10 men in the 68th minute after Bastoni received two yellow cards in three minutes, the second coming after he put his hands in the face of a Shakhtar player in an off-the-ball incident.

Nine minutes later, though, Inter took the lead as a wonderfully worked break ended with Augusto expertly controlling a superb floated pass from Henrikh Mkhitaryan before prodding the ball beyond Dmytro Ryznik.

That marked Shakhtar’s first defeat of the league phase, and Sporting CP also fell from the ranks of the unbeaten teams as they slipped to a stunning 3-2 loss at home to LASK Linz, who claimed their first Champions League win.

Luis Suarez put Sporting ahead from the penalty spot in the fifth minute, only for Christoph Lang to level 10 minutes later.

The turnaround was completed in the 63rd minute when Sasa Kalajdzic capped off a LASK counter-attack to give the Austrian side the lead, which was doubled five minutes later as Krystof Danek fired a superb finish into the bottom corner.

Suarez’s second gave Sporting hope of salvaging a point, but LASK held on to write a wonderful new chapter in their history.

Real Betis maintained their 100 per cent record as Isco’s second-half penalty gave them a 1-0 win over Feyenoord. They are one of just five teams to have taken maximum points from three games.

At the other end of the league phase table, Lille remain without a point following a 4-2 home defeat to Galatasaray.

Yunus Akgun opened the scoring for Gala before a first-half brace from Soriba Diaoune put Lille in front.

However, Alexey Batrakov levelled before half-time and Gala retook the lead early in the second half, Lille goalkeeper Berke Ozer credited with an own goal after he failed to keep out a corner flicked on by Lucas Torreira.

A deflected Victor Osimhen strike sealed the points for Gala, the Nigerian refusing to celebrate as he came back to haunt the club where he made his name.

Lille’s neighbours Lens also tasted defeat as Club Brugge made it two wins from three to start their campaign with a 3-0 victory at the Jan Breydel Stadium.

articles.title: Michael Carrick apologises to Manchester United fans after ‘unacceptable’ Champions League performance
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has once again apologised for his team's performance.
articles.content:
Michael Carrick apologises to Manchester United fans after ‘unacceptable’ Champions League performance

Michael Carrick has once again apologised for his team's performance.

Last Update:

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has apologised to supporters following his side’s disappointing Champions League performance against Como, admitting the display was “unacceptable”.

United travelled to Italy under pressure after a run of six matches without a win, but their latest European outing left Carrick frustrated once more.

The former United midfielder accepted full responsibility for the performance and insisted there could be no excuses for what his players produced.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Carrick delivered a damning assessment of his team’s display.

“It was more than disappointing. I think everybody has got to take responsibility for that,” he said.

“I 100% take responsibility for the overall team and the performance – that’s where it stops. It stops with me and I’m absolutely fine with that. I accept that totally.

“But as a supporter of this football club for so long, to see a performance like that is unacceptable, I have to say.”

Manchester United boss apologises to travelling supporters

Carrick was particularly disappointed for the United fans who had travelled to Italy to support their team.

The 45-year-old stressed the importance of the club’s supporters and admitted he felt compelled to apologise for what they had witnessed.

“I care an unbelievable amount about the supporters,” Carrick said.

“They are the heartbeat of this football club and they always will be. For them to travel, I had to apologise for the performance.

“To have to watch a performance like that, I totally feel for them. There are no excuses at all. It is not acceptable.”

With pressure mounting over his position, Carrick was also asked whether he still had the backing of Manchester United’s board.

However, he refused to discuss his own future, insisting his immediate focus was on assessing the performance.

“It’s not about me. It’s about digesting the game and how it went. That is the most important thing right now.”

articles.title: Virgil van Dijk reveals Mohamed Salah’s role in Rio Ngumoha development as Liverpool star continues to shine
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah had a key role in Rio Ngumoha's development.
articles.content:
Virgil van Dijk reveals Mohamed Salah’s role in Rio Ngumoha development as Liverpool star continues to shine

Mohamed Salah had a key role in Rio Ngumoha's development.

Last Update:

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has praised Mohamed Salah for helping Rio Ngumoha develop into one of the club’s most exciting young players following his impressive performance against Villarreal.

The 18-year-old registered two assists as Liverpool came from 2-0 down to beat the Spanish side 4-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday evening.

Ngumoha has impressed on the right wing this season despite typically playing on the opposite flank, with Van Dijk revealing how Salah’s experience has helped the youngster adapt.

Van Dijk believes Liverpool’s senior players have played an important role in Ngumoha’s progress, highlighting Salah and Cody Gakpo as two particularly influential figures.

“A few senior players [have helped him],” the Liverpool captain said.

“I would say [Cody Gakpo] is definitely part of that. But everyone has that role in order to help the youngsters in the group, the players who have not had so much experience.

“Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo last year was obviously massive as Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities?

“I think he has shown it this season but there is still much more to come.”

Ngumoha was a constant problem for Villarreal’s defence at Anfield, using his pace and movement to help Liverpool recover from their disastrous start.

“He’s pretty electric at times and he showed it again,” Van Dijk added.

“He was a complete threat constantly and their defender had a tough time.”

Liverpool captain admits mistakes against Villarreal

While Ngumoha earned praise for his attacking display, Van Dijk was critical of his own performance.

The Dutch defender made an early mistake which allowed Georges Mikautadze to open the scoring before Sergi Cardona doubled Villarreal’s advantage.

Liverpool eventually fought back through goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Ronald Araujo and Florian Wirtz, but Van Dijk admitted he had made life difficult for his teammates.

“It was a terrible start,” he said.

“I think the saying is you fight an uphill battle and as a defender it is pretty difficult to come back from it. I tried but it was a bad day at the office personally but we did it together with 11 players. We turned it around and that’s the main thing.

“Unfortunately in life these things can sometimes happen. Fortunately it didn’t happen too many times in my Liverpool career but tonight I was not the best.

“But we won and it’s not about me, it’s all about us. We got the three points.”

articles.title: Why me? Kvaratskhelia posts emotional message after ACL blow that will sideline PSG star for rest of the season
articles.summary: PSG winger Kvaratskhelia believes his injury will help protect other players
articles.content:
Why me? Kvaratskhelia posts emotional message after ACL blow that will sideline PSG star for rest of the season

PSG winger Kvaratskhelia believes his injury will help protect other players

Last Update:

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has vowed to come back stronger after sustaining a ruptured ACL and claimed he was chosen by God to help protect other players from injury.

The Paris Saint-Germain winger sustained the setback last night during the 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona at the Parc des Princes, falling awkwardly after challenging Xavi Espart.

He will undergo an operation in the coming days and won’t play again this season.

It is a crushing blow for the 25-year-old and for PSG, who will now go in search of a third successive Champions League success without the brilliant Georgian.

Kvaratskhelia wrote on social media: “Why me? I was not ready for this.

“Many people have asked me questions about this setback, many have said that if all the footballers in the world prayed, the match would end in a draw. That might be true, but before every match I play, I ask God to leave the field unscathed, but in vain.

“It hasn’t been long, but it’s still in my head – why me? I’ve never missed anything, probably prepared for this game the best I’ve ever prepared. I thought I was prepared for everything, but no. I realise that God has chosen me and if I was protecting the players on another field, I’m ready to go through these months of work, pain, tears.

“I know I have to come back stronger for my people who always support me, I won’t let you down, I promise I won’t waste a second. Thank you all for your support, see you soon.”

Kvaratskhelia one of three injury blows for PSG

There was early concern when Kvaratskhelia was helped off just short of the hour mark last night and PSG’s worst fears were confirmed this morning following tests.

A PSG medical update read: “Victim of a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament of the right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery in the coming days.”

The medical update also revealed both Ousmane Dembele and captain Marquinhos sustained thigh injuries that will keep them out for several weeks.

Speaking after the game, PSG boss Luis Enrique admitted his frustration at the prospect of having to do without three key players at an important stage of the season.

“I am not the doctor. I am the coach,” he said. “The three injuries is the worst part of the game today. We will have to wait for the tests tomorrow. They are three very important players, so it’s really bad news, of course, but that’s football.”

It is the loss of Kvaratskhelia that will hurt the Parisians most, though.

The supremely gifted playmaker, nicknamed ‘Kvaradona’ by fans of former club Napoli in homage to the great Diego Maradona, is a major part of PSG’s attacking arsenal.

He has scored 29 goals in 91 games for PSG in all competitions.

articles.content:
Bayern Munich midfielder Kimmich to miss Arsenal game due to family bereavement

Bayern Munich will be without one of their most influential players against Arsenal in the Champions League tonight

Last Update:

Joshua Kimmich will miss Wednesday night’s Champions League game with Arsenal due to a family bereavement, Bayern Munich announced this morning.

The Bayern captain was absent from training yesterday and won’t be considered for the fixture with the Gunners at the Allianz Arena.

A club statement read: “Due to a passing in his immediate family, Joshua Kimmich is not in the squad today for the match against Arsenal.

“On behalf of the family, we ask that his privacy and grief be respected, and that further inquiries and reporting be refrained from.

“We send our deepest condolences to Joshua Kimmich and his loved ones.”

In Kimmich’s absence, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Tom Bischof could form the central midfield pairing for the Bundesliga leaders.

Bayern boss Kompany struggling to be fit for Arsenal clash

Kimmich’s absence continues a disrupted build-up to the game for Bayern, who are without star midfielder Michael Olise through suspension following his red card against Viking in their last Champions League outing.

Coach Vincent Kompany missed Tuesday’s media conference as he battles to shrug off a virus with his assistant Aaron Danks speaking to the press.

Danks said: ”Vincent has a virus. It’s important that he rests. He’s at home resting. We take it day by day. We’re in constant communication. He’ll play his role and part in the game – whether that’s at the Allianz Arena or not, we’ll have to wait and see.

“It has affected his legs at times, he found some pain in his legs. It’s just a virus. The doctors know way more than I do. The most important thing is that he rests and takes the time he needs. I don’t know whether that will be tomorrow or 2-3 days. We’re taking it day by day.

“For me, not much changes. I plan the training sessions every day. Obviously we miss Vincent, but we have a strong coaching team, we know what needs to be done. We need to stay calm and keep the players’ energy high so they are ready tomorrow.”

articles.content:
Andoni Iraola warns Liverpool players ‘cannot relax’ despite fighting back in Champions League win

Andoni Iraola has opened up on a tough night in the Champions League for Liverpool

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has warned his players they cannot afford to switch off against top opposition after coming from behind to beat Villarreal in the Champions League.

The Reds recovered from a difficult first half to secure the win at Anfield, but Iraola was frustrated by his side’s defensive mistakes and admitted they have been conceding too many goals this season.

Speaking to Amazon Prime after the match, the Liverpool boss praised his team’s response while insisting there is still plenty to improve.

“A lot of things happened today. They were much better than us in the first half and we were much better in the second half,” Iraola said.

“When we’ve been under pressure, we answered well. When we relaxed, we made mistakes. You cannot relax against very good opposition. I value the win.

“We have to know that if we don’t go to the limit, it will be difficult. We are facing very good teams. It’s good to come back but we’ve started losing too many goals this season.”

Iraola praises Rio Ngumoha’s development

One positive for Liverpool was the performance of 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha, who continues to earn opportunities under Iraola and registered two assists on Tuesday night.

The manager believes the youngster is becoming a more rounded player, particularly after adapting to a role on the right flank.

“I am really happy wth Rio. He is trying to improve everything that we try to correct,” Iraola said.

“He is playing a lot more on the right and he has adapted really well. He’s going more inside. He struggled defensively in the first half, second half was much better. He’s becoming a more complete oayer. He’s still only 18.”

Last Update:

Champions League headlines

Holders PSG end Barcelona winning run in Parc des Princes thriller

Wirtz on target as Liverpool fight back to beat Villarreal

Man City cruise past AEK

Alvarez earns point for Atletico

Julian Alvarez scored his first goal of the season for 10-man Atletico Madrid as they came from behind to draw 1-1 with Stuttgart in the Champions League.

Stuttgart looked on course for three wins from three to start the league phase when Jamie Leweling drilled home a low effort to break the deadlock in the 36th minute.

However, Alvarez, who failed in his bid to force through a move to Barcelona in the summer, responded two minutes into the second half, finding the top-right corner with a first-time finish from Ademola Lookman’s pass.

Atletico were reduced to 10 in the 64th minute when Morten Hjulmand saw red for an awful challenge on Angelo Stiller. However, Stuttgart could not make their extra man count.

Their Bundesliga rivals Borussia Dortmund bounced back from defeat to Bodo/Glimt last time out as a Serhou Guirassy double gave them a 2-1 win over Sabah in Azerbaijan.

Bodo, meanwhile, made Napoli work extremely hard for their first win of the league phase.

Matteo Politano opened the scoring in Naples after just 53 seconds, only for Bodo to restore parity when Jens Petter Hauge slotted into the bottom-right corner.

Scott McTominay put Napoli in front again in the 41st minute, only for Andreas Helmersen to equalise as Bodo responded once again.

Yet McTominay doubled his tally with a close-range header to give Napoli the lead for a third time, and an own goal from Odin Bjortuft made the points safe for the hosts before Sondre Brunstad Fet pulled one back in stoppage time.

Roma joined Napoli in claiming a first victory of the league phase, thumping Slovan Bratislava 4-0, but it is three defeats from three for Portuguese champions Porto after Guus Til’s effort gave PSV Eindhoven victory at Estadio do Dragao.

Elsewhere, Slavia Prague earned their first point of the phase as Pavel Kacor’s injury-time goal earned them a 2-2 draw at Fenerbahce.

articles.title: Cesc Fabregas hits back at ‘not very nice’ Manchester United job question as Michael Carrick faces growing pressure
articles.summary: Cesc Fabregas has been asked about taking over from Manchester United boss Michael Carrick.
articles.content:
Cesc Fabregas hits back at ‘not very nice’ Manchester United job question as Michael Carrick faces growing pressure

Cesc Fabregas has been asked about taking over from Manchester United boss Michael Carrick.

Last Update:

Como manager Cesc Fabregas has dismissed speculation linking him with the Manchester United job, insisting it is disrespectful to discuss replacing Michael Carrick while he remains in charge.

Fabregas will come up against Carrick on Wednesday evening when Como host United in the Champions League, with the visitors desperate to end a six-match winless run.

The former Arsenal, Chelsea and Barcelona midfielder was asked during his pre-match press conference whether he would consider taking over at Old Trafford.

However, he refused to entertain the suggestion and instead defended his opposite number.

“I won’t answer that question because I think that’s not a very nice question,” Fabregas said on Tuesday.

“I don’t think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side.

“Manchester United is a historical club I know very, very well,” he continued.

“We have so much respect for who they are, for what they do, because they have incredible players.

“I know Steve Holland very well because I worked with him for years at Chelsea and I know Michael has done really well in previous clubs as well.

“Last year he did really well bringing Manchester United back to where they belong, which is the Champions League, for the first time in many years, so it’s not all bad. It’s an honour to host them for the first time in our history.”

While United arrive in Italy struggling for form, Como have enjoyed an encouraging start to their domestic campaign.

Fabregas’ side sit fifth in Serie A and head into Wednesday’s European encounter following a 3-1 win over Fiorentina on Sunday.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho sends Vinicius Junior warning: ‘Only the badge is untouchable’
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has warned Vinicius Junior that his place at Real Madrid is never safe.
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho sends Vinicius Junior warning: ‘Only the badge is untouchable’

Jose Mourinho has warned Vinicius Junior that his place at Real Madrid is never safe.

Last Update:

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has warned Vinicius Junior that no player is guaranteed a place in his starting XI ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash with RB Leipzig.

The Brazilian has endured a difficult start to the season, scoring just once in all competitions, and faces increasing competition for his place from summer signing Yan Diomande.

Vinicius is currently serving a four-match suspension in LaLiga but remains available in Europe, where he struggled during last week’s dramatic 4-3 win over Roma.

He was substituted after 58 minutes, with replacement Endrick helping inspire Madrid’s comeback.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Mourinho made clear that reputation and previous achievements would not guarantee anyone a place in his team.

“Only the badge is untouchable,” Mourinho said.

“I don’t like the concept of ‘untouchable’ players. What makes players untouchable isn’t a captain’s armband, or how long they’ve been at the club, or their status. What makes a player untouchable is performance.”

Mourinho has always supported Vinicius despite his struggles, but recent performances from other attacking players have given the Portuguese manager additional options.

“As I said recently, I’m not a stubborn coach,” he explained.

“There are coaches who have an idea, and live or die by that idea. I’m not that kind of coach, I’m always open to analyse, to understand things and look for the best for the team.”

Mourinho plays down Real Madrid’s Champions League ambitions

Madrid have won their opening two Champions League matches against Inter Milan and Roma, but Mourinho refused to describe his side as contenders for the trophy.

“It’s very early,” he said.

“Right now Real Madrid don’t have the objective of winning the Champions League. We have the objective of qualifying [for the knockout phase].

“Then, if we get the points that allow us to qualify, then we get to our second objective, to try to avoid the playoffs, which are two games with tension, and they’re games you can avoid.”

Madrid also face a big challenge in LaLiga, sitting six points behind Barcelona ahead of Sunday’s Clasico at Camp Nou.
