articles.title: Man City captain Ruben Dias: We do what we do, we win
articles.summary: Ruben Dias says the Manchester City players are fully focused on winning and won't get distracted by the club's off-field issues
articles.content:
Man City captain Ruben Dias: We do what we do, we win

Ruben Dias says the Manchester City players are fully focused on winning and won't get distracted by the club's off-field issues

Last Update:

Ruben Dias says Manchester City will continue to win – and celebrate those victories – despite believing everyone else wants them to fail.

The City captain led from the front on Sunday with another superb display as his side cruised to a 3-0 success at Liverpool in the first game since the club were found guilty of breaching over 100 financial regulations.

City have appealed the verdict and an appeal is ongoing but the ruling from the Independent Commission has brought a wave of condemnation from across the football spectrum.

Dias accepts that has increased the levels of hostility towards City but insists it won’t distract the players from their objectives.

The Portugal defender said: “Yes, there’s a lot of noise, and it’s almost impossible to avoid seeing something – even us, being as private as we can be, and doing just our own lives. On your phone it’s impossible to avoid everything.

“But I feel like we’re all so very good at focusing on our job, doing it right, making the most of it, being happy every time we come to work, and our minds are very much there, and only there. It’s the things we can control, the things we’ve always been doing, and enjoying so much.

“We have full confidence in the club, we trust the club, and we love to win.”

We trust the club, says City skipper Dias

City faced a hostile atmosphere at Anfield, one that will be replicated up and down the country until the matter is closed, but Dias is confident the squad can shut out the distraction of what is going on off the field.

He added: “I feel like when you build yourself as a player, you build yourself against any kind of noise. So be it the one you just described [at Anfield], be it any other kind.

“Personally, and I really feel like I speak for the whole group: We’re very calm. We trust the club, we’re very calm, and we’re very focused on enjoying football. We know the team we’ve got, we want to make the most out of it, we want to win, and that’s the only thing in our minds.

“If there’s more or less noise, or whatever the reason the noise is, at the end of the day it’s the same as before because people don’t love us winning, and we love to win.

“We do what we do, we go on the pitch, we play football, and we win.”

‘Everyone at City is excited for PSG test’

City put their 100% record this season on the line on Wednesday night when two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain are the visitors in the Champions League.

“It’s a massive game, and I believe everyone is excited for it,” he said. “It will be a great time for us to feel ourselves at this level against the best team in Europe at the moment. We’re excited for the challenge, everyone is, the fans – I imagine they can’t wait to be there tomorrow just like us. I think it will be special.”

articles.title: Steven Gerrard demands Manchester City ‘suffer’ as Liverpool legend calls for huge punishment over financial breaches
articles.summary: Steven Gerrard says Manchester City must be made to 'suffer' after breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.content:
Steven Gerrard demands Manchester City ‘suffer’ as Liverpool legend calls for huge punishment over financial breaches

Steven Gerrard says Manchester City must be made to 'suffer' after breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

Last Update:

Steven Gerrard has called for Manchester City to face a severe, long-term punishment following their guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial regulations, insisting the club must be made to “suffer” for the impact on their rivals.

The former Liverpool captain believes a transfer ban and points deductions spread across several seasons would be more appropriate than relegating City to the Championship.

Gerrard’s comments come after City were found guilty of the vast majority of the financial charges brought against them by the Premier League, although the club are appealing the verdict.

The 46-year-old was Liverpool captain when they finished runners-up to City in the 2013-14 Premier League season and believes the consequences of the breaches extend far beyond his own career.

Speaking on Overlap Daily, Gerrard made clear that he wants substantial sanctions imposed on City if the findings are upheld.

“Multi-year punishments, that would be my opinion,” he said.

“I’m not saying that’s the right opinion, but that’s just how I feel sitting here in this chair.

“I think putting them down to the Championship is not fair on the EFL. I don’t think it’s enough, because they’ll bounce back.

“You look at that team yesterday. Can you imagine that in the Championship? With all due respect, it’s not fair on the teams playing against City week in, week out. It’s not fair on the potential team that could be the third team to come up.

“I think it needs to be a transfer ban. I think it needs to be points over a period of time.

“And make them suffer like they’ve made everyone else suffer for the nine, ten years that they’ve done it for. That would be my opinion. But there needs to be an example set.”

Liverpool legend claims City have ‘stolen’ memories from rivals

Gerrard also reflected on Liverpool’s failure to win the Premier League in 2014, when Brendan Rodgers’ side finished two points behind City.

The former midfielder famously slipped during Liverpool’s defeat to Chelsea towards the end of that campaign, a moment that became closely associated with the club’s unsuccessful title challenge.

Despite his personal connection to that season, Gerrard insisted he would not want to receive a Premier League winners’ medal retrospectively.

“It’s not personal for me in terms of the Manchester City players because they’re all outstanding players,” he explained.

“They have lived a moment and they obviously deserved to… I’m not somebody who is going to sit here and say I would accept a Premiership medal or I want one that they have got.

“I think I have come to terms with that I have never won the Premier League, that I was short in that department in terms of winning it.

“What about the memories they have taken away from not just possibly me, and the team that I played in but over that period of time, nine, ten years?

“Spurs fans, United fans, Everton fans, teams at the bottom, teams in the cups?

“City, ex-players, current players, and City owners, everyone connected with City have got to think about the memories they have stolen away from everyone else.”

articles.title: What do you want us to do? Maresca dismisses criticism of Man City’s Anfield celebrations
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca says Manchester City had every right to celebrate the win at Liverpool on Sunday
articles.content:
What do you want us to do? Maresca dismisses criticism of Man City’s Anfield celebrations

Enzo Maresca says Manchester City had every right to celebrate the win at Liverpool on Sunday

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca has defended Manchester City’s celebrations that followed the weekend win at Liverpool and admitted they continued in the dressing room.

The game at Anfield was City’s first since an Independent Commission ruled the club had breached 114 financial regulations. City continue to deny any wrongdoing and have appealed the verdict but the issue continues to leave a stain over the English game.

City’s players showed no signs of distraction on Sunday with a superb performance and victory that was celebrated with gusto in front of their travelling fans at the final whistle.

Many observers felt a low-key approach would have been more suitable given the circumstances but Maresca felt the smiles were justified.

Speaking ahead of Wednesday night’s Champions League game with Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad, he questioned why his players’ response was criticised, stating: “Criticised for what? We won 3-0 at Anfield. What do you want us to do? And even if it was 1-0, it would be exactly the same.

“I’m here today, and the players are here today, to win tomorrow’s game. And we work every day to win games. It’s the only thing, again, that we can think [about] and be focused on.

“The rest? It’s just things from outside that we need to deal with, but we were so, so, so happy inside the pitch, and you cannot imagine inside the changing room.”

Liverpool win was special for the City fans – Maresca

Maresca said sharing the win with the City fans was special given what they would have gone through over the past fortnight.

He added: “Probably it has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me. Probably because it’s more complicated because if I am an Arsenal fan or a United fan, and you are a Man City fan, I can tell you, ‘Hey my friend, you cheat’, or these kind of things.

“So probably it has been more tough for them, but again, we were happy at the end of the game. Inside the changing room we were very happy, celebrating the three points because we know how difficult it is at Anfield.”

City skipper Ruben Dias echoed Maresca’s sentiments, adding: “I very much stand by the manager’s words, as well. It’s a win at Anfield. In whatever circumstances, so be it now maybe earlier in the season, so be it later in the season, any time – I and we will enjoy it just as much, and we will celebrate it however it feels in the moment, and it will obviously be a show of how much it means to us.

“Whenever you win, there’s people not happy with it because they have the same ambition, they want to win as well. We do what we do, we go on the pitch, we play football, and we win.”

We know the seriousness of the situation – City boss Maresca

Maresca says he and his players are fully aware of the potential consequences that could be coming City’s way despite the club putting on a remarkable show of solidarity since the Independent Commission’s ruling.

“I said many times, I am a completely calm, relaxed,” he added. “I promise you I stress a lot about gameplans and how we can train every day, but I don’t stress about things that I don’t control.

“So, the message with the players will be exactly the same as I said, we know the seriousness of the situation but at the same time it is not something that we can do something about. Where we can do things is on the pitch so that is why I like to focus there and the message to the players is exactly the same.

“I said after the Liverpool game that the noise around the team is a big noise but we need to try to deal with that and try to make our noise, which is to win games.”

City’s perfect record will be tested by PSG

City have won every game they have played this season but that record will be given the stiffest test on Wednesday against the two-time defending European champions.

And Maresca admitted this season’s Champions League carries added significance given it may be the last time City compete at Europe’s top table for a while.

He said: “For sure, the Champions League for this organisation is so important, no doubt.

“We are going to try to improve, compared to the last two, three years where the club, the team struggled a little bit.

“So, we are going to try to do our best to improve that. Again, where we can be in March, April or if this is the last Champions League for a while, I don’t know.

“We are, for sure, a good team, no doubt. Where we are in this moment compared to PSG? I don’t know.

“I know how good they are because in the last two years they won the last two Champions Leagues – that shows how good they are but at the same time, again, I don’t know if we’re close, far, but for sure, we are a good team.”

articles.title: Ange Postecoglou praises Cristiano Ronaldo after Al-Nassr star caught up in Saudi Arabia missile threat
articles.summary: Al-Nassr head coach Ange Postecoglou has praised Cristiano Ronaldo for his professionalism following the missile threats in Saudi Arabia.
articles.content:
Ange Postecoglou praises Cristiano Ronaldo after Al-Nassr star caught up in Saudi Arabia missile threat

Al-Nassr head coach Ange Postecoglou has praised Cristiano Ronaldo for his professionalism following the missile threats in Saudi Arabia.

Last Update:

Ange Postecoglou has praised Cristiano Ronaldo and his Al-Nassr team-mates for their professionalism after a missile threat in Saudi Arabia forced their Asian Champions League match to be delayed by an hour.

The former Tottenham manager admitted he was concerned about his players after a ballistic missile was intercepted near Riyadh on Monday, triggering security alerts across the Saudi capital.

Despite the disruption, Ronaldo scored his 981st career goal as Al-Nassr secured a 3-1 win over Uzbekistan side Neftchi Fergana.

The 41-year-old also made a public show of support for Saudi Arabia following the match, kissing the Al-Nassr badge and celebrating with supporters.

Postecoglou admitted the safety and wellbeing of his players had been his biggest concern after reports of an imminent missile attack raised doubts about whether the match could go ahead.

“I was concerned about how the players felt during the match,” the Australian said.

“But I was absolutely delighted with the professionalism they showed to ignore what had happened and get on with playing football.

“And I would like to thank the Al-Nassr fans for their continued support in difficult times. It is greatly appreciated.”

The comments came after a Saudi-led military coalition confirmed it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired towards Riyadh by the Houthi movement.

The incident prompted widespread concern in the city, with residents receiving emergency alerts on their mobile phones.

The match at Al-Awal Park had originally been due to begin at 9.15pm local time, but broadcasters subsequently announced a one-hour delay.

Supporters inside the stadium were informed that the situation was safe and asked to remain in their seats while authorities assessed the threat.

Ronaldo scores 981st career goal despite Riyadh security alert

Ronaldo was among the players caught up in the disruption but responded by helping Al-Nassr secure an important win.

His strike took his remarkable career tally to 981 goals, leaving him just 19 away from becoming the first player to reach the 1,000-goal milestone.

Ronaldo’s performance also came just days after another controversial episode involving the Portugal national team.

The veteran striker recently left his country’s international camp following a disagreement with manager Jorge Jesus over his playing time.

He subsequently apologised for his actions and was provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation while disciplinary proceedings continue.

Ronaldo’s actions following Monday’s match attracted further attention as he demonstrated his affection for the country he has called home since January 2023.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward kissed the crest on his Al-Nassr shirt before leading supporters in a post-match Viking clap.

articles.content:
Real Madrid legend joins Getafe on season-long deal

Dani Carvajal has joined Getafe on a deal until June

Last Update:

One of Real Madrid’s most decorated players, Dani Carvajal, has signed for Getafe.

The right-back left the Santiago Bernabeu in June when his contract expired, bringing an end to his 24-year association with the club.

His final couple of years were disrupted by injuries but he will get the chance to extend his career further after agreeing a deal with Getafe that will see him play for the club until at least the end of the season.

Carvajal won 27 trophies with Real Madrid, including six Champions League crowns, and was a member of the Spain squad that clinched the European Championship in 2024.

Former Real Madrid hero will being ‘experience and leadership’ to Getafe

A Getafe statement read: “Getafe CF has reached an agreement with Dani Carvajal, linking him to the azulón club until June 30, 2027.

“Having been capped 51 times with the Spanish national team and with an extensive career in elite football, Carvajal embarks on a new chapter in his sporting career in the south of Madrid where he will bring experience and leadership.

“From Getafe CF, we want to welcome Dani Carvajal and wish him much success in this new stage. Welcome to the Coliseum, Dani!”

Getafe are 14th in La Liga and play host to Rayo Vallecano on Monday night.

Carvajal can look forward to an emotional return to Real Madrid on January 3.

articles.title: Champions League Predictions: More misery for Manchester United, Arsenal stroll while Liverpool get much-needed win
articles.summary: It's round two of the Champions League and there are some mouth-watering ties to look forward to, including Manchester City hosting Paris Saint-Germain.
articles.content:
Champions League Predictions: More misery for Manchester United, Arsenal stroll while Liverpool get much-needed win

It's round two of the Champions League and there are some mouth-watering ties to look forward to, including Manchester City hosting Paris Saint-Germain.

Last Update:

It was a fascinating weekend of Premier League football – and yet how much of it really mattered?

Manchester City’s ongoing battle to clear their name after being found guilty of over 100 breaches of financial regulations means there is an asterisk next to everything until any sanctions are announced and confirmed.

That doesn’t really apply to the Champions League although it would bring into sharp focus the level of City’s wrongdoing if they were to reclaim the trophy they last won in 2023.

Enzo Maresca’s side are involved in the tie of the matchday when they host two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.

Here, we take a look at the week’s key games and offer our predictions.

TUESDAY

Arsenal v Lille (8pm)Arsenal struggled again at the weekend, requiring goals in the final half hour to see off Leeds at the Emirates. Indeed, with some better finishing, the Yorkshire side would have headed back up the M1 with all three points. Mikel Arteta insists he is happy with his side’s attacking output but there’s no doubt they are not currently firing on all cylinders. Arteta is likely to make a few changes for the visit of Lille and he may find answers elsewhere in his deep squad. Lille are going well in Ligue 1 and sit just a point behind leaders Monaco. Davide Ancelotti has proved elite management runs in the genes but this is a huge test for the 37-year-old.Prediction: Arsenal 3-0 Lille

Atletico Madrid v Manchester United (8pm)Despite conceding a last-gasp equaliser against Tottenham on Saturday, a point was arguably more than Manchester United deserved after another largely lifeless performance. Teams often mirror their manager and, at the minute, United are quiet, unassuming and lacking aggression, just like Michael Carrick. Carrick has some major issues to address and the Metropolitano is not the ideal place to do it. Atletico will smell blood and Diego Simeone is not one to let that opportunity pass.Prediction: Atletico Madrid 2-0 Manchester United

Galatasaray v Barcelona (8pm)The real test of Hansi Flick’s Barcelona will likely come in the Champions League this season. They already seem nailed on to retain La Liga for a third successive year with main challengers Real Madrid limping along having taken the backward step of reappointing Jose Mourinho over the summer. Barca have not lifted Europe’s elite club trophy since 2015 but should challenge this season. Rodri is a shrewd acquisition but the lack of a world class number nine could eventually prove problematic. Galatasaray will look to make it difficult for the Catalans, as will a boisterous home support at RAMS Park. This won’t be straightforward but Barca should have enough.Prediction: Galatasaray 1-3 Barcelona

WEDNESDAY

LASK Linz v Liverpool (5.45pm)Liverpool performed well for 20 minutes against Manchester City on Sunday but you always sensed they would run out of steam. That’s exactly what happened and, assisted by the unfortunate dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, the visitors ran away with it. Liverpool have yet to solve the Florian Wirtz conundrum with the Germany international looking totally lost again at the weekend. Bradley Barcola was equally poor and Reds fans have every right to expect more. LASK are also struggling having not won in the Austrian Bundesliga since September 1. Prediction: LASK Linz 0-1 Liverpool

Aston Villa v Fenerbahce (8pm)Like Liverpool and Manchester United, Aston Villa are stumbling through games right now. Saturday’s home draw with Brentford was a decent result after another disjointed display. Perhaps we should not expect anything else after a summer of upheaval at Villa Park and it is likely Unai Emery will need time to mould this latest incarnation of Villa into a cohesive unit. Fener have plenty of Premier League experience in their ranks with the likes of Ederson, Nathan Ake, N’Golo Kante, Romelu Lukaku and former Villa loanee Marco Asensio. It remains to be seen whether the visitors are willing to subject Mason Greenwood to a hostile return to England.Prediction: Aston Villa 1-1 Fenerbahce

Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain (8pm)There seems very little contrition at Manchester City, although that is perhaps understandable given their absolute confidence their name will be cleared. That is likely to lead to a sense of defiance at the Etihad on Wednesday night against the two-time defending European champions. On the pitch, City have been superb with Enzo Maresca making a seamless transition into the hot seat vacated by Pep Guardiola. This is a huge test, though. PSG may have won just half their games in Ligue 1 but they will still win the title. They save their best displays, and best XIs, for nights like this.Prediction: Manchester City 2-1 Paris Saint-Germain

Roma v Real Madrid (8pm)Jose Mourinho could do with some love right now. The former Roma boss will be assured of a warm welcome back at the Stadio Olimpico and will relish the chance to get away from the Spanish capital after another weekend of controversy that saw him skip his post-match media duties following the 1-0 win over Villarreal. The drama that follows him is regarded as box-office by some and hugely tedious by others. His team have shown themselves to be vulnerable away from home this season with defeats at Atletico and Real Betis and will be tested again by a Roma side going well in Serie A.Prediction: Roma 1-2 Real Madrid

articles.title: Lampard hails ‘complete performance’ as Jaissle left frustrated by Newcastle attack
articles.summary: It was a night to remember for Frank Lampard and Coventry.
articles.content:
Lampard hails ‘complete performance’ as Jaissle left frustrated by Newcastle attack

It was a night to remember for Frank Lampard and Coventry.

Last Update:

Frank Lampard hailed a “complete performance” from Coventry City after they claimed their first home Premier League win since 2001 with a 4-1 victory over Newcastle United, whose boss Matthias Jaissle was left frustrated by their play in the final third.

Promoted Coventry got off the mark before the international break with a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest, but they entered Monday’s clash still without a goal at the CBS Arena.

That changed in the sixth minute when Jack Rudoni opened the scoring from the penalty spot following an error from Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Newcastle dictated proceedings thereafter and saw several chances to equalise go begging, with the Magpies punished for their profligacy as Sidiki Cherif doubled Coventry’s lead three minutes into the second half.

Sven Botman gave Newcastle hope of a fightback with a stunning 70th-minute strike, and a fourth goal looked more likely to come from the visitors as they pushed for a leveller.

But a defensive error from Lewis Hall allowed Ellis Simms to restore a two-goal lead for Coventry with a deflected strike, before Stephen Mfuni fired in off the post to round off a memorable night for the Sky Blues.

“Very, very satisfying,” Lampard told Sky Sports of Coventry’s performance.

“It’s so hard to win. We played like the team that we want to be here. There is so much spirit and energy in the group and we know we are going to have to suffer a lot this season.

“The work ethic of the boys and the belief, you get what you deserve which is great finishes. We haven’t quite had that rub of the green this season that would help us nick more points.

“It was a complete performance. we have to keep our feet on the ground. It’s a great feeling for the players to feel that.

“It was a long 20 minutes [after the Botman goal] and it’s a fantastic strike but we also did some good defensive work. That was a worry but we started to make some changes and that’s when you are asking for good lads that train all week to come on and add to the performance.

“If we don’t have that spirit, we haven’t got a chance. We need everybody. A lot of the lads knew that tonight.”

Jaissle apologises to Newcastle fans

While Coventry scored four goals from six shots on target, Botman’s goal was Newcastle’s only reward for a performance in which they had 66.7 percent possession and had 19 shots on goal, six of them on target.

Jaissle indicated his irritation at the lead-up to the second goal, for which Joe Willock was off the field following a collision that led to him leaving the field for treatment but was not given as a foul, but accepted his side were not good enough in attacking areas.

“We’re frustrated definitely,” Jaissle said to Sky Sports. “It’s a feeling you don’t want to have when you feel as though you should have won. We can only apologise to the fans that took the journey.

“We need to analyse it clearly, especially in the box, at both ends. The desire and hunger to score, to finish the attacks, that was missing.

“The second goal there was a foul on Joe Willock but it wasn’t whistled, in my eyes, he was then missing in that spot where the ball dropped after the throw in. We need to improve the things we can control.

“It’s never nice to concede a goal but we had the approach after half time to come out and turn it around. The lads believed so we made the first goal and momentum was on our side.

“That’s something also we need to learn that in a risk zone you cannot lose the ball. You cannot invite the opposition to score the third one, then it’s going to be difficult.

“We need to win these games in the boxes. Defensively we need to improve. On the offensive we need to be more sharp.”

articles.title: ‘We’re embracing the challenge’ – Carrick not feeling Man United pressure as Shaw and Mainoo ruled out
articles.summary: United have made their worst league start for 40 years.
articles.content:
‘We’re embracing the challenge’ – Carrick not feeling Man United pressure as Shaw and Mainoo ruled out

United have made their worst league start for 40 years.

Last Update:

Michael Carrick insists he is not feeling any added pressure because of Manchester United‘s dismal start to the Premier League season.

United were held to a 1-1 draw at home to 10-man Tottenham on Saturday, Dominic Solanke equalising late on for Spurs despite Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card, Bryan Mbeumo having seemingly put Carrick’s men on course for victory.

The Red Devils have taken just six points from their opening six Premier League games, marking their worst start to a league season since the 1986-87 campaign.

More troubling than the result against Tottenham was the nature of the performance at Old Trafford, where United were second best for long periods and were grateful for Spurs’ profligacy in the final third.

The display raised the scrutiny on Carrick in his first season as permanent manager after an excellent interim spell last term.

United boss: I love when it’s going against you

But Carrick, who confirmed United will be without both Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid, is undaunted by the seemingly mounting external pressure.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference, Carrick said: “Depends how you define pressure. We know what we want and what we expect.

“That comes from us. I know what it looks like, I don’t feel the pressure from that, I want to win and succeed. There’s no negativity, we’re embracing the challenge.

“There’s going to be times when it’s a struggle and if you can’t do something difficult and get through it you’re not going to succeed.

“It’s fine lines. We didn’t start well the other day. The late goals we’ve conceded have all be avoidable but it’s fine margins.”

Asked if he is surprised by how quickly things have gone wrong, Carrick replied: “We expected a lot more. I knew there was going to be a period where it became stickier. That’s part of it.

‘It’s a journey, there will have been times when it’s not gone to plan for Atletico, they’ve had success but it hasn’t all been in one direction.

“I understand people thinking it’s a disaster but that’s not in our mindset. You’ve got to be able to deal with it.

“The last three goals we’ve conceded we could have done something about them. That can be the difference. I love this part when it’s going against you. The fans are there and we’ve got to give them something. We will come through it.

“They [the players] care. We’re here to test ourselves. If you don’t want to dig deep it’s not the place for you.

“I’ve seen it behind closed doors and in the changing rooms. It’s a big week, two tough games but we’re looking forward to them. We’ll come out fighting.”

United visit Leeds United on Sunday in another testing league fixture, with the injuries to left-back Shaw and midfielder Mainoo far from ideal for Carrick’s side as they face a difficult week.

“They’ve not travelled, both picked up issues in the game at the weekend so they’re out,” Carrick said of that pair.

On striker Benjamin Sesko, who has not featured since the EFL Cup defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion on September 16 because of a shin issue, Carrick explained: “We’re still waiting for a few extra tests. We need to be on top of it. We haven’t got a timeframe [for his return].

articles.title: Flick hails Gabriel Jesus as ‘perfect’ for Barcelona amid Raphinha absence
articles.summary: Jesus already has three goals since joining from Arsenal.
articles.content:
Flick hails Gabriel Jesus as ‘perfect’ for Barcelona amid Raphinha absence

Jesus already has three goals since joining from Arsenal.

Last Update:

Hansi Flick believes Gabriel Jesus is “perfect” for Barcelona following the striker’s impressive start to life at Camp Nou.

Jesus joined Barcelona from Arsenal in September, having seen the final years of his time in North London heavily disrupted by injury.

Barca spent much of the summer trying to prise Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, with their failure to do so seemingly leaving the defending LaLiga champions light at the centre forward spot.

But the signing of Jesus to help fill that void following Robert Lewandowski’s departure to MLS side Chicago Fire is looking an increasingly astute one.

With Raphinha, who had been playing through the middle, out with a thigh injury, Jesus made it three goals in five games in all competitions by scoring the second goal in Barcelona’s 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday.

Before Tuesday’s Champions League clash at Galatasaray, Flick heaped praise on the former Manchester City striker.

Asked about the possibility of Jesus starting against Galatasaray, Flick told a pre-match press conference: “Yes, of course he’s ready. He’s ready to play. But if he plays, we don’t know yet. We will see. We will decide tomorrow after the training today.

“But I’m very happy that he’s in our team. It was a little surprise, to be honest. But at the end, he’s absolutely a top guy.

“He’s a very good player for us. Very good player for us. And his behaviour, his character, it’s perfect for us. It’s a great guy.”

Barcelona had a comfortable start to their latest effort to win the Champions League for the first time since 2015, beating Feyenoord 5-1 in their league phase opener.

But Flick knows the task in Istanbul is likely to be considerably more difficult.

“We have to be prepared for the atmosphere. It’s one of the best in the world,” Flick added.

“It’s incredible. The sound of the stadium is incredible. They have improved a lot against great teams and we have to be united.

“I always say I’m happy with how we started, but every game is different. It’ll be tough tomorrow.

“It’s a privilege to be here. We’re all ready for this game.”

articles.title: ‘If I had another penalty I’m going to take it’ – Gabriel undeterred by Champions League shootout woe
articles.summary: Gabriel will face old club Lille on Tuesday as Arsenal continue their campaign to win the Champions League for the first time.
articles.content:
‘If I had another penalty I’m going to take it’ – Gabriel undeterred by Champions League shootout woe

Gabriel will face old club Lille on Tuesday as Arsenal continue their campaign to win the Champions League for the first time.

Last Update:

Arsenal defender Gabriel would not hesitate to take another penalty in a Champions League final despite missing the decisive spot-kick in their defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last season.

Gabriel blazed his effort over the crossbar as PSG retained the title on penalties after the final ended 1-1 after extra time.

The Gunners started their campaign to go one better with a 1-0 win at Napoli last month and, before Tuesday’s visit from his former club, Lille, Gabriel made it clear he would step up again should they find themselves in another shootout on the biggest stage in European football.

“In a final, anything can happen,” Gabriel told a pre-match press conference. “We did really well.

“In the Champions League, of course if I had another penalty I’m going to be there to take it. My team-mates helped me a lot after this.

“I was sad – I don’t want to miss a penalty – but I’ve learned from this and if I have another opportunity I’m there to take it.

“We are really happy to be in the Champions League again. We want to keep the momentum; last year, we did really well. It’s an opportunity for us again to attack the Champions League.

“We are very motivated – we want to attack every trophy – and tomorrow we are going to have another opportunity to play in the Champions League and at home in front of our people. We are ready to go.”

Arsenal bounced back from their 3-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion immediately before the international break by coming from behind to beat Leeds United 2-1 at home on Saturday.

They remain three points behind leaders Manchester City, and Gabriel is satisfied with how Mikel Arteta’s men have begun the season.

“It’s how we want to be – we have a good mentality every game.” he added. “We started the season really strong so we need to keep pushing and keep believing in us.”

And he is relishing the visit of Lille, whom he left in 2020 to join Arsenal.

“It’s going to be a very special day for me,” said Gabriel.

“I have a lot of love for LOSC, especially to see the fans and play against [them] I am really happy to see them.”

articles.title: Arteta pleased with Arsenal’s attacking flow despite stumbling displays
articles.summary: Arsenal are not firing on all cylinders at the moment but Mikel Arteta is confident they will regain top form, starting on Wednesday against Lille
articles.content:
Arteta pleased with Arsenal’s attacking flow despite stumbling displays

Arsenal are not firing on all cylinders at the moment but Mikel Arteta is confident they will regain top form, starting on Wednesday against Lille

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta is not concerned by Arsenal’s stuttering form and says their attacking output is “going pretty well” ahead of Tuesday night’s Champions League game at home to Lille.

The Gunners remained within three points of Premier League leaders Manchester City with a 2-1 home win over Leeds on Saturday but it required goals in the final half-hour to see them over the line, Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes on target.

For the first 60 minutes, Arsenal were second best with Leeds’ 3-5-2 formation frustrating the hosts and also giving the visitors joy on the counter attack.

But the defending champions found a way to successfully bounce back from the 3-0 hammering at Brighton before the winter break.

Asked whether he felt his side’s attacking flow had diminished in recent games, Arteta said: “I think it is going pretty well. I think the way we have finished the actions is probably something we need to improve, but in terms of what we produced before the international break it was better than any other year.

“Then we had obviously the Brighton game, then the other game [against Leeds] which was a different context as well. But we are getting in good positions and we just need to be more clinical now to finish more actions.”

Even though the performance was a little patchy, the victory over Leeds was another triumph for Arsenal’s strength of character

“We have to be emotionally dominant regardless of what the context is, which is easy to say but actually very difficult to do,” said Arteta. “We did it in the majority of the matches, which is great. We didn’t do it in Brighton and we paid the penalty of that.”

Arteta confirms double injury blow for Arsenal

Saturday’s win was not without its issues, albeit after the game, not during.

In the training session that followed, both Piero Hincapié and Martin Zubimendi sustained injuries that mean they won’t be available against Lille.

Arteta added: “We had a training session planned for after the game for players that did not have enough minutes, and in two very unfortunate actions we lost two players. Not great.

“We need to assess them today and have further scans to see where they are then we will have a timeframe on how long they are going to be out for.

‘If they never train then they don’t get injured, but the consequence to that is when they are needed to play they have no rhythm and when you ask them to play they are going to have no impact in the game.

“That could happen at the Emirates – it never happened in seven years that I have been here. It could happen the next day in the training session. That has happened before and hopefully it doesn’t happen again.

“What can you do? If I had a crystal ball I would just say ‘guys, get in the Jacuzzi and I will see you tomorrow’.”

Arteta praises Eze despite being Arsenal’s forgotten man

Zubimendi’s injury may move Eberechi Eze up the pecking order with the England international not getting off the bench at the weekend. Eze has yet to start a league game this season but Arteta says his attitude has been “phenomenal”.

“Like everybody else I think they need to earn the right to play,” said the Spaniard. “That’s up to training sessions and when you are on that pitch to have the impact on the game that the team needs, in order to achieve that.

“He [Eze] is going to have many opportunities to do that. His attitude is phenomenal and our players have to adapt as well to his qualities.”

Arteta confirmed centre-half William Saliba is back in training following a back problem but remains some weeks away from a first-team return.

articles.title: ‘Best goalkeeper in world’ Courtois set to sign new deal at Madrid
articles.summary: Thibaut Courtois has said he could stay at Madrid until he is almost 40
articles.content:
‘Best goalkeeper in world’ Courtois set to sign new deal at Madrid

Thibaut Courtois has said he could stay at Madrid until he is almost 40

Last Update:

Thibaut Courtois is poised to sign a contract extension at Real Madrid to keep the goalkeeper at the club until 2028, according to a report.

Two-time Champions League winner Courtois, 34, joined Los Blancos from Chelsea for £35 million in 2018 and has shone at the start of head coach Jose Mourinho’s second spell in charge.

Courtois’ current contract expires at the end of the campaign but the Belgium international has reached a verbal agreement on new terms, transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano has said.

Why Real Madrid have given Thibaut Courtois a new contract

Madrid spent £223 million this summer but Courtois has been arguably their most important player during their first eight league matches of the season and made seven saves in their 2-1 home win over Inter in their Champions League opener.

Mourinho’s side faced 12 second-half attempts at home to a dangerous Villarreal team on Saturday but earned a 1-0 win in a result that already looks vital with leaders Barcelona six points ahead of their most familiar title rivals, who have lost twice in the 2026/27 Liga.

Courtois made four saves during the game and prevented 0.87 goals, according to Sofascore, who also pointed out his value as a partial sweeper, taking 46 touches and completing 25 of 36 passes.

Thibaut Courtois injuries: How long will he stay at Madrid?

Real Madrid have continued to trust Courtois but the decision to only give him a one-year extension may reflect the series of injury problems suffered by their most reliable goalkeeper.

Courtois, who has said he wants to stay for at least four more years, has missed 32 matches for Madrid and Belgium since returning from a knee injury that kept him out between August 2023 and March 2024.

While at Chelsea, Courtois was also sidelined for 20 club and international games in late 2015 with his first major knee injury.

Thibaut Courtois and Jose Mourinho

Mourinho inherited Courtois during his second spell in charge of Chelsea between 2013 and 2015 and the pair won the 2014/15 Premier League title together, with Courtois becoming an English champion again in 2016/17.

“I have a very good relationship with Jose Mourinho,” Courtois has said. “It’s always been very good.

“We’ve also had our clashes. Mourinho is a very direct manager and I’m the same.”

Mourinho was effusive in his praise when Courtois congratulated Anatoliy Trubin after his counterpart scored a sensational last-gasp goal against Madrid to keep the Portuguese’s former side in the Champions League in January.

“What Courtois did with Trubin was out of this world,” said Mourinho. “Within the sadness of defeat, he found a few seconds to rejoice for [Trubin], who did something extraordinary.

“I didn’t have time to realise what Courtois did. I’m not surprised, because he was my player. He is the best goalkeeper in the world.

“With this attitude, he proved that he will go down in the history of the Champions League as a great, no matter what happens. What he did is incredible.”

Courtois called the incident a “nice moment” he “wanted to share” with Trubin. “It was something natural and just a cool moment for him,” Courtois told UEFA.

Thibaut Courtois stats, saves

Courtois has already conceded as many goals as he did last season but his save percentage so far matches the second-best season of his career, figures from AS show.

“He has made the extraordinary look routine, making save after save,” the outlet said.

“But he is also busier than ever. He is up to his neck in work.”

Thibaut Courtois career history

These are the club Courtois has played for.

Thibaut Courtois Real Madrid trophies

Here’s a look at Courtois’ key achievements with Madrid.

What’s next for Thibaut Courtois and Real Madrid?

Courtois’ next appearance could come in the Champions League on Wednesday, when Madrid play their second match of the league phase at Italian side Roma (20:00 BST / 15:00 ET / 12:00 PT).

“The way we want to play is with rhythm, control and pressing after losing the ball,” Courtois said earlier this season.

“If we manage to do that in every game, we are in for a great year. But for that, everyone has to work hard for 90 minutes.

“I also hope everyone stays healthy, which is the most important thing.”

articles.title: Enzo Maresca sends ‘togetherness’ message to Manchester City fans after Liverpool win
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca has spoken after Manchester City's 3-0 win over Liverpool
articles.content:
Enzo Maresca sends ‘togetherness’ message to Manchester City fans after Liverpool win

Enzo Maresca has spoken after Manchester City's 3-0 win over Liverpool

Last Update:

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has praised his players for overcoming a hostile atmosphere at Anfield and suggested the club’s ongoing off-field problems could help strengthen the relationship between the team and its supporters.

City secured an important Premier League win over Liverpool despite struggling during the first half, with Maresca admitting his side initially found it difficult to cope with the intensity of the occasion.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Maresca was asked whether City’s ongoing off-field issues could bring the players and supporters closer together.

“Probably yes, probably no. I don’t know,” the City boss said.

“It can create togetherness with the fans. I said during the week bring the passion, bring the noise and hopefully we can celebrate a win. This is the only thing we can focus on.

“After 10-15 years where the organisation is winning titles, doing the right things in terms of winning titles and then this happens it’s not a good feeling for them.

“There is a process ongoing, this is not the moment.

“I can not control things outside football so why stress?” he said.

“I stress about gameplan, day by day training sessions but the rest it’s not in my hands.”

Maresca tells City players to embrace hostile atmospheres

Maresca admitted Manchester City had struggled to impose themselves during the first half against Liverpool, particularly when they were out of possession.

“Very difficult circumstances, difficult environment,” he said.

“We struggled first half, we were on the ball but not so much off the ball.

“Second half we made some adjustments and we were much better. In the build-up we were not doing the right things, second half we were better.”

The City manager also highlighted the challenge of playing at Anfield, where Liverpool’s supporters created an intimidating atmosphere.

However, he believes his players must become accustomed to such occasions.

“We need to learn how to deal with the noise because the noise will be with us at all of our away games – there will be noise,” Maresca explained.

“We need to deal with that and make our noise. Our noise is to win games.

“The feeling at the end of the game with our fans and our noise, that’s a nice feeling and a different noise.”

“It was nice to play this kind of game for the noise, the environment. We need to make our noise and deal with their noise.”

articles.title: ‘Call it karma’: Glasner takes responsibility for Forest defeat at Palace
articles.summary: The Austrian admitted it was a "crazy" contest in south London.
articles.content:
‘Call it karma’: Glasner takes responsibility for Forest defeat at Palace

The Austrian admitted it was a "crazy" contest in south London.

Last Update:

Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner described his side’s defeat at his former club Crystal Palace as “karma”.

Forest were beaten 3-1 on Glasner’s first return to Selhurst Park since leaving Palace in the summer after leading them to FA Cup and Conference League glory.

Dan Ndoye opened the scoring for the visitors inside the first 5 minutes and for the next 35 minutes it was one-way traffic.

Liam Delap wasted two great chances to extend the advantage before out of seemingly nothing Palace levelled through Daichi Kamada.

The comeback was complete on the stroke of half-time when Jefferson Lerma bundled home a corner, while Yeremy Pino secured the points shortly before the hour mark.

Glasner gives reaction to ‘crazy’ game

Speaking after the match, Glasner admitted his side had failed to “kill the game off”, but insisted his players “did everything” to try to get a result.

“We didn’t kill the game off and we should have done it, creating so many chances,” Glasner said.

“I played many games here [Selhurst Park] and I haven’t seen a team create so many chances.

“At the end, we did not convert them. We conceded the two goals before half time then we had two big chances but then we conceded the slapstick goal and we are 3-1 down.

“Today it looks like it is just me who is responsible for this, call it karma or whatever but it was like I didn’t deserve to win at Selhurst Park because the players did everything. Nobody to blame for anything, the effort was there and the quality was there.

“This performance will give us confidence even if it feels strange with the result. Crazy game but for us it is important not just to look at the result.”

Next up for Forest is the visit of defending champions Arsenal on Sunday, while Palace travel to France to play Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday before facing Brighton in the so-called M23 derby next weekend.

articles.title: Watch: Ndoye gives Forest early lead but Palace hit back
articles.summary: It was one-way traffic for most of the first half, but the hosts fought back.
articles.content:
Watch: Ndoye gives Forest early lead but Palace hit back

It was one-way traffic for most of the first half, but the hosts fought back.

Last Update:

Dan Ndoye produced a clinical finish to give Nottingham Forest the lead inside the opening five minutes of their Premier League clash with Crystal Palace.

The Switzerland international pounced on an error from Anan Khalaili before stroking the ball into the far corner on what was, for the first 40 minutes at least, a happy return to Selhurst Park for Forest boss Oliver Glasner.

The visitors were dominant from the off, and should have extended their advantage before the break when Morgan Gibbs-White’s effort from distance cam back off the bar to the feet of Liam Delap.

But with the entire goal to aim at, the Forest striker blasted a volley straight at Palace keeper Walter Benitez, who threw his body in the way to somehow prevent the ball from crossing the line.

Delap again squandered a chance moments later when he diverted his back-post header the wrong side of the post.

The missed chances would prove costly. Having rarely ventured into Forest’s defensive third, Palace drew level on 40 minutes when Daichi Kamada prodded home entirely against the run of play.

The first-half comeback was complete when Jefferson Lerma bundled in from an Adam Wharton corner after Matz Sels had just moments earlier made a brilliant save from Tyrick Mitchell.

articles.title: Ten-man Southampton edge out Portsmouth in south-coast derby
articles.summary: It was a first win for Saints in this fixture in more than two decades.
articles.content:
Ten-man Southampton edge out Portsmouth in south-coast derby

It was a first win for Saints in this fixture in more than two decades.

Last Update:

Ten-man Southampton held on to earn all three points – and, perhaps just as crucially, bragging rights – in the south-coast derby with fierce rivals Portsmouth in the Championship.

At an unsurprisingly raucous St Mary’s Stadium, James Bree netted what proved to be the only goal of the game after 20 minutes, finishing well after being picked out impressively by Finn Azaz.

The Saints’ task was made all the more difficult when Cameron Bragg was dismissed for a second yellow on the stroke of half-time.

After the break, Portsmouth, with the man advantage, pushed for an equaliser, but as tempers began to flare as the clock clicked closer to full-time, the visitors were unable to break down their hosts.

It was the first league victory for either side in this fixture for 21 years, and a first league win for Southampton in the derby for 22 years.

Eckert: Spygate scandal ‘changed my life’

The result comes at the end of a week when Southampton boss Tonda Eckert admitted the club’s Spygate scandal “changed my life”.

The 33-year-old was handed a suspended six-week suspension on Wednesday following his involvement in the Saints secretly filming a Middlesbrough training session towards the end of last season.

However, he avoided an immediate touchline ban and so was able to be in the dugout as they saw off their bitter rivals Pompey.

The win sees Southampton, who maintain their perfect league record at home this term, move up to 11th in the second tier, while Portsmouth languish down in 19th.

articles.title: Messi bags brace in first game since Argentina farewell
articles.summary: The 39-year-old was on the scoresheet as Inter Miami won comfortably against DC United.
articles.content:
Messi bags brace in first game since Argentina farewell

The 39-year-old was on the scoresheet as Inter Miami won comfortably against DC United.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi scored twice in his first since game since his emotional Argentina farewell as Inter Miami ran out comfortable winners over DC United in the MLS.

The 39-year-old, who scored in his final appearance for his national team in Buenos Aires earlier this week, netted a second-half brace in his club side’s 4-0 win.

Veteran striker Luis Suarez was also at the double to lift Miami into second place in the Eastern Conference.

The former Liverpool and Barcelona forward opened the scoring inside three minutes, sweeping home from a cross after being left unmarked in the DC penalty area.

Suarez doubled the advantage seven minutes before half-time when he bundled home after Messi’s initial effort had been saved.

Messi makes his mark

The Uruguayan then turned provider after the break, clipping the ball to Messi who poked the ball past Sean Johnson in the DC goal to make it three.

Thirteen minutes later, Messi helped himself to the pick of the goals when, after receiving the ball on the edge of the penalty box, he danced past several DC defenders before calmly finishing into the corner of the net.

Messi’s goals take his MLS goals tally for the season to 23, as he hopes to claim what would be a third straight league MVP award.

Kily Gonzalaz, Miami’s coach, had earlier this week urged fans to appreciate the talents of his compatriot while they still can.

“He’ll be missed in that [Argentina] jersey, of course, but today we have him here, and we have to enjoy having him with us now,” Gonzalez said.

articles.title: Carrick hurt by Old Trafford boos as Manchester United’s poor start continues
articles.summary: Fans were less than impressed by Man Utd's display
articles.content:
Carrick hurt by Old Trafford boos as Manchester United’s poor start continues

Fans were less than impressed by Man Utd's display

Last Update:

Michael Carrick admitted he was hurt by boos from sections of the Manchester United supporters after slipping to a late 1-1 draw at home to winless Tottenham.

Dominic Solanke’s late header cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo’s finish at Old Trafford in a game where the visitors enjoyed many of the better chances, with some supporters making their feelings known at half-time and full-time with audible boos.

“It’s not nice,” Carrick told Sky Sports.

“It hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

Carrick admitted United were poor in the first half but felt they grew into the game and acknowledged that late goals are affecting them significantly.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through.

“We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.

“I don’t think it is lack of confidence, but a game can get away from you very quickly. We found a way right back into the game, and got ourselves in a great position – that is one of the most disappointing things.”

Match Statistics

Mbeumo: First half wasn’t us

Goalscorer Mbeumo said United’s first half was not up to scratch but was keen to take the positives from the draw.

He added: “We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

articles.title: De Zerbi ‘happy’ after seeing ‘right spirit’ as Spurs climb off bottom but winless start continues
articles.summary: Spurs climbed off the bottom of the table but are still winless
articles.content:
De Zerbi ‘happy’ after seeing ‘right spirit’ as Spurs climb off bottom but winless start continues

Spurs climbed off the bottom of the table but are still winless

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi was pleased with Tottenham’s display at Manchester United after fighting back with 10 men to earn a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford.

Dominic Solanke scored a header in the second minute of added time to earn a point they were good value for after seeing a host of excellent chances missed against the Red Devils, who went ahead through Bryan Mbeumo.

Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card meant Spurs had to show even more spirit to get back into the game, and De Zerbi was pleased to take the positives despite their winless start to the season ultimately stretch to six games.

De Zerbi told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four.

“The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat.

“We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

De Zerbi: ‘There aren’t too many strikers better than Solanke’

De Zerbi was full of praise for goalscorer Solanke, who was selected as captain for the game at Old Trafford, and insisted there are few better No9s in the league after opening his account for the season.

The Italian added: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke.

“Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

articles.title: Premier League round-up: Ipswich pile more misery on Fulham as Brighton charge on with win over Sunderland
articles.summary: Catch up with the best of the action from the Premier League's afternoon games.
articles.content:
Premier League round-up: Ipswich pile more misery on Fulham as Brighton charge on with win over Sunderland

Catch up with the best of the action from the Premier League's afternoon games.

Last Update:

Sunderland 0-2 Brighton

Brighton overcame a second-half red card to beat Sunderland 2-0 at the Stadium of Light, with Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scoring for the visitors.

The Seagulls played more than 30 minutes with 10 men after Pascal Struijk was sent off, but Sunderland failed to capitalise on their numerical advantage.

Both sides struck the woodwork during an entertaining first half. Wilson Isidor turned Enzo Le Fee’s cross against the post before Struijk headed Pascal Gross’ free-kick onto the upright shortly before the interval.

Brighton broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute when Gross collected a quick throw-in and found De Cuyper, who took a touch before finishing past Robin Roefs.

However, the visitors suffered a setback four minutes later when Struijk was dismissed following a VAR review for denying Isidor a goalscoring opportunity.

Sunderland pushed forward in search of an equaliser, with Granit Xhaka testing Bart Verbruggen from a free-kick before Malick Fofana saw an effort comfortably saved.

Brighton defended well despite their numerical disadvantage and sealed the win in stoppage time.

Substitute Georginio Rutter released Hadjam down the left, and the defender marked his Premier League debut with a composed finish across Roefs to secure all three points.

Ipswich 2-1 Fulham

Ipswich scored twice in the closing minutes to secure a 2-1 win over Fulham at Portman Road, with Dara O’Shea heading home the winner in stoppage time.

Fulham had looked set for their first Premier League win under Alvaro Arbeloa after Ryan Sessegnon’s superb strike, but Gary O’Neil’s side produced a remarkable comeback.

The visitors enjoyed the better chances before half-time, with Christian Walton denying Sander Berge before Gonzalo Garcia dragged an effort wide.

Fulham eventually broke the deadlock in the 55th minute when Sessegnon collected a half-clearance from Issa Diop and fired a brilliant left-footed effort into the bottom corner.

Ipswich responded strongly, with Emersonn heading against the post before Bernd Leno produced an excellent save to deny Sindre Walle Egeli.

The hosts finally equalised in the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara controlled Calvin Bassey’s clearance and hammered a stunning long-range strike past Leno.

Three minutes later, Jack Clarke delivered a dangerous free-kick and O’Shea headed home at the near post to complete the turnaround.
